data.title: Wrench Attacks: Physical attacks targeting cryptocurrency users (2024) [pdf]
data.author: pulisse
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：加密货币持有者遭遇绑架等犯罪事件的增加及其原因和应对措施

不同观点：
• Adrig: 最近法国发生了两起加密货币相关绑架事件，表明这种情况会变得更糟且更难防范。大多数事件是由“业余”犯罪者实施的，这使得这些事件更加不可预测。
• _tom_: 分享了一篇关于纽约地区加密货币投资者遭遇事件的链接，显示此类事件在其他地方也在发生。
• thasso: 质疑为何拥有传统（非加密）资产的富人较少遭遇此类事件，是否因为他们更低调或有银行等保护措施。
• TheAmazingRace: 强调加密货币持有者应保持低调，不要透露自己的财富，因为伪匿名性和个人密钥的脆弱性使得持有者容易成为目标。持有者应避免讨论自己的资产，因为人性脆弱，容易受到暴力威胁。
• lo0dot0: 认为将这类事件称为“新颖”是自负的，因为人类互相抢夺财物已有数世纪历史。
• imaginator: 提供了Jameson Lopp维护的物理比特币攻击列表链接，并开玩笑说由于通货膨胀，XKCD的5美元扳手攻击已不再可能。
• akrymski: 质疑银行是否仍有其价值。
• jonfromsf: 建议投资于持有比特币的ETF，在传统经纪账户中进行交易，这是最直接和安全的方式。
• anigbrowl: 认为这种情况不需要学术论文来解释，富人如果缺乏良好的个人安全措施且炫耀自己的加密货币财富，自然会成为犯罪分子的目标。
• pluto_modadic: 希望讨论能与YubiKeys攻击或记者在边境被拘留等事件有相似之处。
• specialist: 质疑 stealing crypto 的可行性，并讨论了混币器在隐藏资产链方面的有效性，指出即使在俄罗斯、朝鲜或金三角等地区，最终还是会有实际的冲突。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及了对加密货币持有者为何容易成为目标的原因分析，包括其财富的公开性和伪匿名性。
• 提出了应对措施，如保持低调、投资传统金融产品等。
• 争议的焦点在于如何有效保护加密货币持有者的安全以及加密货币的伪匿名性是否足够安全。
• 对 stealing crypto 的可行性和技术细节进行了探讨，特别是混币器和区块链技术的实际应用。

通过这些观点，可以看到讨论的核心在于加密货币持有者面临的安全威胁及其应对策略，涉及到技术、社会工程学和个人行为等多方面因素。

data.title: 'Strange metals' point to a whole new way to understand electricity
data.author: pseudolus
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对文章中关于准粒子模型、电子行为以及电阻与超导性关系的不同观点和讨论。

不同观点：
• elcritch认为文章对研究人员超越准粒子模型的描述很有趣，并将研究人员的进展比喻为挣脱束缚的大象。他赞赏新的实验方法，如“聆听”电子扰动，并指出理论家需要实验数据来避免陷入死胡同。
• dinfinity指出量子场论早已将粒子视为场的激发状态，并对文章未提及这一点表示惊讶。
• bawana关注电子自旋及其在超导性和电阻变化中的作用，提出外部磁场是否会影响超导转变温度或电阻率斜率的问题。
• nonelog引用Qimiao Si的话，强调奇怪金属中新物理现象的存在，认为这是显而易见的。
• kens对文章中电阻率曲线形状的描述感到困惑，询问是二次曲线还是指数曲线。
• sfink将超导性比作电子流动，并用液体流动作比喻，探讨电阻与电子速度之间的关系，但未得出明确结论。
• est用牛顿摆作比喻，试图理解准粒子的概念，表示对文章内容的不确定性。
• baerrie对材料研究中测量纠缠的实际应用感到兴奋，并好奇其他具有线性温度变化的材料。
• countWSS将电子行为比作波粒二象性的光子，并根据文章推测在奇怪金属中电子的粒子属性是否消失，只剩下“电子场”梯度。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是文章对电阻率曲线的描述不一致，kens指出了这一点。
• 另一个值得注意的讨论点是量子场论中粒子描述的视角差异，dinfinity对此提出了批评。
• 自旋在电子行为中的作用以及外部磁场的影响是bawana提出的重要问题，值得进一步探讨。
• 不同评论者对文章中提到的准粒子模型和电子行为的比喻和理解方式各不相同，显示出对复杂物理概念的多样解读。

data.title: Design Pressure: The Invisible Hand That Shapes Your Code
data.author: NeutralForest
data.article_summary: 本文总结了一次名为“设计压力：塑造代码的无形之手”的演讲，讨论了为何即使遵循最佳实践，软件架构仍可能变得怪异。作者分享了相关材料和文章，如不同类型的耦合、吸引人的设计陷阱、通过类型设计使非法状态不可表示等。此外，还推荐了一些视频和书籍，如《Tidy First?》、《Architecture Patterns With Python》和《Domain-Driven Design》等，以帮助深入理解软件设计。文章还提及了一些关于类行为、ORM和异步编程的思考，并提供了进一步学习的资源和个人联系方式。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕软件设计、领域模型与数据库设计之间权衡的讨论，以及对具体设计实践的不同看法。

不同观点：
• loevborg：认为在项目初期采用“面向数据库的设计”是合理的，因为初期对领域理解有限，直接引入领域模型可能导致过度设计。随着对领域的理解加深，再逐步引入领域模型和显式映射。这种方法强调在项目的不同阶段进行重构，而不是一开始就追求过多的抽象。

• knallfrosch：分享了在一个全新项目中面临的问题，即在没有现有数据和API的情况下，仍然需要为未来可能的变化做准备。这表明即使在绿地项目中，考虑未来的需求和系统的演化也是必要的。

• g958198：强调设计压力是驱动代码架构最重要的因素，且这种感知是基于直觉的，无法轻易传授或量化。设计决策应考虑系统的长期演化和外部压力，而非仅仅依赖“最佳实践”。

• da39a3ee：对一些具体的技术选择（如attr.ib和attr.s）持批评态度，并认为领域驱动设计（DDD）有时像是一种空洞的潮流。

补充讨论：
• HappMacDonald：提到希望将演讲内容转换为文章形式，因为视频中的口语化内容和旁白在书面阅读时显得不合适。

• vinipolicena：提到演讲内容让他想起了Amundsen's Maxim网站上的观点，暗示可能有相似的设计理念。

• leecommamichael：认为现代开发工具和实践可能鼓励了某种程度的耦合，导致一些开发者缺乏对更广泛架构的理解。

• Noumenon72：提到有人暗示演讲中含有对SQLModel的批评，但自己并未在幻灯片中找到相关内容，且该评论后来被删除，显得有些奇怪。

争议焦点：
• 关于何时以及是否应该在项目初期引入领域模型存在不同看法。loevborg认为初期应避免过度抽象，而knallfrosch则强调即使在绿地项目中也应为未来做准备。
• 对具体技术选择和设计理念（如DDD和某些Python库）的批评和认同，显示出在技术社区中对“最佳实践”的不同理解和接受程度。

44087844.article_content:
Ever had this weird gut feeling that something is off in your code, but couldn’t put the finger on why? Are you starting your projects with the best intentions, following all best practices, and still feel like your architecture turns weird eventually?
So far, I’ve held it at
PyCon US 2025
in Pittsburgh, USA.
Slides on SpeakerDeck
.
Design Pressure: The Invisible Hand That Shapes Your Code
(Sorry for the literal throat-cleaning in the video – I lost my voice the night
before and worked on fumes and Fisherman’s Friends.)
Additional material
Some of the material was referred to directly in the talk but landed on the cutting floor due to time constraints.
They all are highly recommended reading/watching for the topic of software design writ large, though.
Articles
Types of Coupling
by Ben Orenstein
Attractive nuisances in software design
by Paul Ganssle
Designing with types: Making illegal states unrepresentable
by Scott Wlaschin
The Vietnam of Computer Science
by Ted Neward (spoiler: it’s ORMs)
A summary by Jeff Atwood (Coding Horror)
Approximating Sum Types in Python with Pydantic
by William Woodruﬀ
How I Build
by Adam Montgomery
DTOs & Mapping: The Good, the Bad, and the Excessive
by Derek Comartin
An example of a conscious decision process on when to map data and reinforcing my point that it’s a trade-off.
The Typestate Pattern in Rust
by Cliff L. Biffle
This is about Rust, but the concept applies the same to any other language.
What Color is Your Function?
This article argues against async primitives in languages because it causes you to have two different types of functions that behave differently. I don’t fully agree, but I find it interesting to apply this logic to classes.
Arguably, ORM classes and, to a much lesser degree, Pydantic classes, behave very differently than regular classes. Especially, because setting attributes implies I/O which complicates reasoning.
In other words, you have to be aware what kind (color!) of class you’re dealing with when reading code.
Videos
Integrated Tests Are A Scam
by J.B. Rainsberger
The Deep Synergy Between Testability and Good Design
by Michael Feathers
SOLID Principles? Nope, just Coupling and Cohesion
by Derek Comartin
The Rising Sea
by Matthew Drury
Advent of Code
Łukasz Langa’s Keynote PyCon US 2022
Simple Made Easy
by Rich Hickey
Watch it before you call anything “simple” ever again.
Building Protocol Libraries The Right Way
by Cory Benfield
Introducing
Sans I/O
, which is a very related topic about writing I/O-agnostic network protocol libraries.
Functional Core Imperative Shell
by Gary Bernhardt
What Gary calls
Core
, is business logic.
Domain Modeling Made Functional
by Scott Wlaschin
Also available as a
book
.
Books
Tidy First?
by Kent Beck
Very short and very good.
Architecture Patterns With Python
by Harry Percival and Bob Gregory
I will recommend this book in every talk until I die.
Domain-Driven Design: Tackling Complexity in the Heart of Software
by Eric Evans
This is a thicc, dense book that brings the whole domain modeling topic to its logical conclusion. It’s a great read for advanced developers, the DDD community feels sometimes a tad cultish, though.

data.title: Writing a Self-Mutating x86_64 C Program (2013)
data.author: kepler471
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了自我修改程序的概念，这种程序在运行时会改变自己的代码。虽然这种做法不常见，且因调试困难、硬件依赖性和代码复杂性而不被推荐，但它具有学术研究价值。文章详细介绍了如何在Linux系统中通过改变内存页权限，使得程序的代码段在运行时可写，从而实现自我修改。具体步骤包括使用`mprotect()`函数更改内存页权限，并通过反汇编工具查看和修改函数的机器码。文章以一个简单的C程序为例，展示了如何通过修改汇编指令来改变程序的行为。需要注意的是，这种技术主要用于学术探索，实际应用中可能被恶意软件利用。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：自修改代码（self-modifying code）的技术、应用及其挑战

不同观点：
• [积极体验] @ivanjermakov 分享了在SIC-1游戏中编写自修改程序的积极体验，强调了其作为单指令编程游戏的独特性。
• [资源分享] @Cloudef 提到了Kaze Emanuar的视频“Optimizing with Bad Code”，该视频也简要介绍了自修改代码。
• [技术研究] @xixixao 研究了macOS上可执行文件在ARM架构下的表现，特别关注增量编译的性能优化，指出在macOS上通过JIT进行页面重映射是当前实现该目标的唯一方法，但存在挑战。
• [潜在优化] @alcover 认为自修改代码可能在运行时优化中带来巨大好处，尽管调试难度很大。
• [格式赞赏] @oxcabe 对某篇文章的排版和内容组织表示赞赏，认为其结构清晰，有助于理解复杂的技术内容。

补充讨论：
• [Common Lisp视角] @pfdietz 指出在Common Lisp中，生成、编译和执行新代码的程序并不特殊，可以通过构建lambda表达式并调用编译函数来实现。
• [系统限制] @belter 提出在OpenBSD中，由于W^X（Write Xor Execute）机制，自修改代码可能无法工作。
• [技术质疑与细节] @Someone 对某篇文章中自修改代码示例的可靠性提出质疑，指出其在多个方面（如架构依赖、编译器优化、指令缓存处理等）存在潜在问题，并提出为何示例中未处理指令缓存刷新问题。

争议焦点：
• 自修改代码在不同平台和系统上的可行性和限制，例如在OpenBSD上的W^X机制下的不可行性。
• 自修改代码示例的技术细节和假设的可靠性，特别是在不同编译器优化和系统环境下的表现。

44089106.article_content:
âWhy would you ever want to write a program that changes its code while itâs running? Thatâs a horrible idea!â
Yes, yes it is. Itâs a good learning experience though. This is not something you would ever do outside of exploring a curiosity.
Self-mutating/self-modifying programs arenât useful for a whole lot. They make for difficult debugging, the program becomes hardware dependent, and the code is extremely tedious and confusing to read unless you are an expert assembly programmer. The only good use for self-mutating programs in the wild I know of is as a cloaking mechanism for malware. My goal is purely academic so I venture into nothing of the sort here.
Warning: This post is heavy on x86_64 assembly of which I am no expert. A fair amount of research went into writing this and itâs possible (almost expected) that mistakes were made. If you find one, send an email so that it may be corrected.
The first step of writing a self-mutating program is being able to change the code at runtime. Programmers figured out long ago that this was a bad idea and since then protections have been added to prevent a programâs code from being changed at runtime. We first need to understand where the programâs instructions live when the program is being executed. When a program is to be executed, the loader will load the entire program into memory. The program then executes inside of a virtual address space that is managed by the kernel. This address space is broken up into different segments as illustrated below.
In this case, weâre only concerned with the text segment. This is where the instructions of the process are stored. Behind the address space are pages which are handled by the kernel. These pages map to the physical memory of the computer. The kernel controls permissions to each of these pages. By default, the text segment pages are set to read and execute. You may not write to them. In order to change the instructions at runtime, weâll need to change the permissions of the text segment pages so that we write to them.
Changing the permissions of a page can be done with the
mprotect()
function. The only tricky part of
mprotect()
is that the pointer you give it must be aligned to a page boundary. Here is a function that given a pointer, moves the pointer to the page boundary and then changes that page to read, write, and execute permissions.

;

return

}
If we give this function a pointer that points to an address in the text segment, that page in the text segment will now be writeable. It is important to note that the OS may refuse to allow the text segment to be writeable. Iâm working on Linux, which does allow for writing to the text segment. If you are using another OS, make sure youâre checking the return value to see if the call to
mprotect()
failed. In the examples below, we assume that the function weâll be changing is contained entirely on a single page. For long functions, this may not be the case.
Now that we can write to the text segment, the next question is: what do we write?
Letâs start with something simple. Say I have the following function:

data.title: Lisping at JPL (2002)
data.author: adityaathalye
data.article_summary: 本文讲述了Lisp语言在喷气推进实验室（JPL）的兴衰历程，重点描述了1988年至1991年期间，作者参与自主移动机器人项目的工作经历。当时，JPL正在规划火星探测任务，大型探测器是主流，但作者的导师David Miller主张使用小型探测器，并通过创意筹资雇佣了Colin Angle开发小型机器人Tooth，与大型的Robby形成对比。Lisp是当时AI开发的主要语言，Robby和Tooth都使用Lisp编程。尽管Robby运行Lisp，但Tooth由于内存限制，使用了专门的Lisp编译器生成6811代码。后来，作者开发了ALFA语言，用于编程Rocky系列机器人，最终应用于火星探路者任务的Sojourner探测器（该探测器改用C语言编程）。尽管这段时间JPL在机器人研究上取得显著成果，但由于组织内部斗争，机器人智能小组最终解散，大部分成员离开。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Lisp语言在JPL（喷气推进实验室）的兴衰以及其在现代软件开发中的地位和应用

不同观点：
• 作者[lisper]指出，原文已经过时，并提供了一个更新的链接。他表示欢迎大家提问（AMA），展现出对讨论的开放态度。
• [neuroelectron]分享了在亚马逊工作时，Lisp代理在内部网络监控中的应用，暗示了Lisp在某些大公司中的秘密应用，但未说明当前是否仍使用。
• [hatmatrix]认为，Lisp在早期选择中非常有意义，但2001-2004年后，其他主流语言在团队协作和维护遗留代码库方面更有优势，尽管他本人是Lisp的粉丝。
• [adityaathalye]引用了1994-1999年期间远程代理调试的故事，强调了Lisp在特定应用场景中的独特价值。
• [adamgordonbell]提供了一个包含图片的版本链接，展示了对Ron Garrett的采访，进一步介绍了Lisp在JPL的历史。
• [anthk]推荐了一个极简的Lisp版本，认为其比SICP和Scheme更容易学习，并提出了Forth作为另一种合适的选择。
• [jmclnx]认为Lisp在JPL的消亡是一个悲剧，并质疑当前学校是否仍教授Lisp，表达了对过去多种语言共存环境的怀念。
• [dragochat]对Lisp在过去如Google的20%时间项目中的应用表示怀念，并希望AI的崛起能重新振兴Lisp。

补充讨论：
• [anthk]进一步讨论了极简Lisp和Forth的实现，提供了相关资源链接，并展示了如何在资源受限环境中实现这些语言。
• 争议焦点在于Lisp在现代软件开发中的适用性，尤其是在团队协作和维护遗留代码库方面的劣势，与其在特定场景中的独特优势之间的对比。

总体而言，讨论围绕Lisp的历史应用、当前状态及其在现代环境中的潜在价值展开，参与者提供了不同的视角和个人经验。

44059994.article_content:
Lisping at JPL
Copyright (c) 2002 by Ron Garret
(
f.k.a. Erann Gat
),
all rights reserved.
This is the story of the rise and fall of Lisp at the Jet Propulsion
Lab as told from my personal (and highly biased) point of view.  I am
not writing in my official capacity as an employee of JPL, nor am I in
any way representing the official position of JPL.  (This will become
rather obvious shortly.)
1988-1991 - The Robotics Years
I came to JPL in 1988 to work in the Artificial Intelligence group on
autonomous mobile robots.  Times were different then.  Dollars flowed
more freely from government coffers.  AI Winter was just beginning, and
it had not yet arrived at JPL.  (Technology at the Lab tends to run a
few years behind the state of the art :-)
JPL at the time was in the early planning stages for a Mars rover
mission called Mars Rover Sample Return (MRSR).  In those days space
missions were Big, with a capital B.  The MRSR rover was to weigh nearly
a ton.  The mission budget was going to be in the billions of dollars
(which was typical in those days).
Against this backdrop I went to work for a fellow named
David Miller
,
who also happened to be my thesis advisor.  Dave had the then-radical
idea of using small rovers to explore planets instead of big ones.  In
1988 that was a tough sell.  Very few people believed that a small rover
could do anything useful.  (Many still don't.)
Using some creatively acquired R&D funding, Dave hired Colin Angle (then
a grad student working for Rod Brooks at MIT, now CEO of IS Robotics) as
a summer student.  Colin built
a small robot named Tooth
,
which stood in very stark contrast to the 2000-pound
Robby
,
which was the testbed for the MRSR mission.
At the time it was more or less taken for granted that AI work was done
in Lisp.  C++ barely existed.  Perl was brand new.  Java was years away.
Spacecraft were mostly programmed in assembler, or, if you were really
being radical, Ada.
Robby had two Motorola 68020 processors running vxWorks, each with (if
memory serves) 8 MB of RAM.  (This was considered a huge amount of RAM
in those days.  In fact, the Robby work was often criticized for, among
other things, being too memory-hungry to be of any use.)  Tooth, by
contrast, had two Motorola 68hc11 8-bit microcontrollers each with 256
bytes of RAM and 2k bytes of EEPROM.  (In later robots we used 6811's
with a whopping 32k bytes of RAM.)
(As an indication of just how fast and how radically attitudes can
change, the other day I heard an engineer complain that "you can't
do
anything
with only 128 megabytes.")
Both Robby and Tooth were programmed using Lisp.  On Robby we actually
ran Lisp on-board.  The Lisp we used was
T 3.1
which was ported
from a Sun3 to vxWorks with a great deal of help from Jim Firby, who
came to JPL from Yale.  Jim also wrote a T-in-common-lisp compatibility
package called Common T.  Using Common T we could do code
development on a Macintosh (using Macintosh Common Lisp and a Robbie
simulator, also written by Jim) and then run the resulting code directly
on Robby with no changes.
Tooth's processors didn't have nearly enough RAM to run Lisp directly
[1]
so instead we used a custom-designed compiler
written in Lisp to generate 6811 code.  At first we used Rod Brooks's
subsumption compiler, but later I decided I didn't like the constraints
imposed by the subsumption architecture and wrote my own for a language
called ALFA
[2]
.  ALFA was subsequently used to
program a whole series of rovers, the
Rocky series
, which
eventually led to the
Sojourner
rover
on the Mars Pathfinder mission. (Sojourner had an Intel 8085
processor with 1 MB of bank-switched RAM.  It was programmed in C.  More
on this decision later.)
Tooth, Robby, and the Rocky series were among the most capable robots of
their day.  Robby was the first robot ever to navigate autonomously in
an outdoor environment using stereo vision as its only sensor.  (NOTE:
The stereo vision code was written in C by Larry Matthies.)
Tooth was only the second robot to do an indoor object-collection task,
the other being
Herbert
, which
was developed a year or two earlier in by Jonathan Connell working in
Rod Brooks's mobot lab at MIT.  (But Tooth was vastly more reliable than
Herbert.) The Rocky robots were the first ever microrovers to operate
successfully in rough-terrain environments.  In 1990,
Rocky III
demonstrated a fully autonomous traverse and sample collection mission,
a capability that has not been reproduced to my knowledge in the twelve
years since.
The period between 1988 and 1991 was amazingly productive for autonomous
mobile robot work at JPL.  It was also, unfortunately, politically
turbulent.  Dave Miller's group was, alas, not part of the
organizational structure that had the "official" charter for doing
robotics research at JPL.  The result was a bloody turf battle, whose
eventual result was the dissolution of the Robotic Intelligence group,
and the departure of nearly all of its members (and, probably, the

data.title: Plwm – An X11 window manager written in Prolog
data.author: jedeusus
data.article_summary: **plwm** 是一个用 Prolog 编写的 X11 窗口管理器，具有高度可定制性，专注于动态平铺窗口管理。其主要特点包括易于配置和修改，使用声明式的 Prolog 语言进行设置；支持多种平铺布局和浮动窗口；轻量级，内存占用仅10-15MB；支持多显示器、外部状态栏（如 polybar）、工作区动态操作等功能。安装需依赖 Xorg 和 SWI-Prolog，通过修改 `.xinitrc` 文件或使用显示管理器配置启动。用户可通过 Prolog 代码定义窗口行为，实现高度个性化的窗口管理。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Prolog语言在实际项目中的应用及其在窗口管理器中的使用

不同观点：
• raron认为Prolog在教程和实际项目中的应用差别很大，从简单的例子过渡到复杂项目时会遇到无限递归和无法解决的问题，表明Prolog在实际应用中的难度。
• eikenberry希望有人能为Wayland写一个窗口管理服务，用协议取代合成器API，以便用任何语言实现窗口管理器。
• major505对Prolog在实际项目中的使用表示惊讶，尤其是用来写窗口管理器，并对Prolog的一般使用表示质疑。
• Jerry2关注是否有用JS和CSS实现的窗口管理器，或允许使用这些技术进行窗口管理和装饰的窗口管理器。
• rabiescow用幽默的方式批评一些人坚持使用X11，而不愿接受新的变化。
• 5-作为Prolog的外行，质疑该项目是否真正利用了Prolog的逻辑特性，或者只是使用了其功能性子集，并讨论了Prolog作为非逻辑功能语言的优点。
• smikhanov对项目源代码的简洁表示赞赏。
• YeGoblynQueenne对项目的文档和整体印象表示赞赏，并有意尝试。
• bolangi对与plwm类似的窗口管理器感兴趣，希望了解其灵感来源。
• jimmaswell在Gentoo上安装并编译了项目，但遇到问题，只得到一个鼠标光标和黑色屏幕。
• B1FF_PSUVM提到这让他想起全Erlang的HN首页，可能暗示对特定语言项目的兴趣或趋势。
• leephillips对项目的实现表示赞赏，但指出由于其使用工作区而非标签，不能替代dwm。
• gatane开玩笑地建议用Scheme实现一个类似的项目。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及Prolog在实际项目中的挑战和复杂性，以及对不同编程语言和技术的偏好和应用场景的讨论。
• 对窗口管理器的实现技术及其可用性的关注，尤其是对JS和CSS等web技术的兴趣。
• 对开源项目文档和代码简洁性的赞赏，以及在实际安装和使用中遇到的具体问题。
• 对不同窗口管理器的功能和设计理念的比较和评价。

About
plwm is a highly customizable X11 dynamic tiling window manager written in
Prolog
.
Main goals of the project are: high code & documentation quality; powerful yet easy customization; covering most common needs of tiling WM users; and to stay small, easy to use and hack on.
Powered by
SWI-Prolog
Feature highlights
Easy to hack on, great way to introduce yourself to the logic programming paradigm and Prolog
Easy to configure: Prolog is declarative, so even though the config is source code, it feels like a dedicated format
Tiling is dynamic, with various layouts included by default: monocle, vertical/horizontal stacks, grid, left/right/top/bottom/centered master-stack, nrows(N), ncols(N)
Floating windows are also supported (move/resize with mouse)
Support for external bars, e.g. polybar, lemonbar
Nice level of EWMH compilance -
partially still work-in-progress
Performance: plwm is fast and light as a feather when it comes to resource usage (10-15 MB memory)
Dynamic workspace operations: create, rename, reindex or delete workspaces on the fly
Other features: multi-monitor support, inner/outer gaps, menu integrations with dmenu/rofi, rules, hooks, animations, command fifo and more
You can say: "My window manager is a semantic consequence of a set of axioms and implications which my computer is deducing/proving from an infinitely branching proof-tree"
Installation
Dependencies:
xorg
with
libx11-dev
,
libxft-dev
,
libxrandr-dev
(exact package names may vary)
SWI-Prolog
(downloadable from most distros' package repos)
On Ubuntu 22.04, easiest way to install them is:
$ sudo apt install xorg-dev swi-prolog
Run:
$ make && sudo make install
By default, this will install plwm to
/usr/local/bin/
. The location can be adjusted in the
Makefile
.
Minimal environment
Add the following line to the end of your
~/.xinitrc
:
exec plwm
Then simply use the command
startx
in tty.
For example, to automate this after logging in, put these lines in
~/.bash_profile
(or to whatever shell startup that matches your setup):
#
Start X from login shell on tty1 if not already started
if
[
-z
"
$DISPLAY
"
-a
$(
tty
)
=
"
/dev/tty1
"
]
;
then
exec
startx
fi
Using a display manager
Please refer to the documentation of your display manager on how to set up sessions for custom WMs.
Here
you can find good references for this.
For most modern display managers, you'll have to create a
/usr/share/xsessions/plwm.desktop
file with content like:
[Desktop Entry]
Name
=plwm
Comment
=This session logs you into plwm
Exec
=plwm
Icon
=path-to-this-repo/plwm/img/logo.png
Type
=Application
Usage
Basics
Command-line options are listed by running
plwm -h
. The manual plwm(1) also contains them as well as the default keybindings.
If you have already used dynamic tiling WMs like dwm, then nothing should be too surprising in this section.
All windows are
managed
by default. This means that whenever a window spawns, it will be added to a list. We call this list the
stack
. Also, the placement and the size of the windows are automatically calculated and set. This is determined by the currently active
layout
(stack, horizontal stack, grid, etc.).
Some layouts are called "master-stack" layouts (the ones which have "master" in their names, e.g.,
lmaster
). With these layouts the first
nmaster
number of windows (1 by default) in the stack go to a dedicated area. These are the
master windows
, which usually have the most space allocated for them. All other windows go to the remaining screen space.
For example, if you start plwm with the default config, you have:
layout = lmaster
,
nmaster = 1
,
mfact = 2/3
, which means that the stack's top window will always be on the left side and occupy 2/3 of the screen width, while the other windows will be in a secondary stack on the right having 1/3 of the screen width.
Some base promises of this approach:
Declarative window management: you only
tell
your system
what
window arrangement you want and don't do the movement/resizin

data.title: Advice to Tenstorrent
data.author: lexoj
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了如何通过简化代码来有效访问Tenstorrent的计算资源。作者George Hotz（geohot）对Tenstorrent的硬件优势和当前问题进行了分析，强调需要增强硬件的可编程性以在AI计算中取胜。他建议从驱动程序和运行时环境开始优化，并指出运行时应保持应用无关性，仅处理编译、调度和排队等任务。对于编译器部分，他主张减少不必要的抽象层，并以tinygrad为例，说明如何处理内存分配和操作调度。最后，作者对ELU（指数线性单元）函数的实现提供了具体建议，强调性能优化的关键。整体而言，文章旨在通过精简和优化代码结构来提升Tenstorrent的竞争力。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对Tenstorrent及其技术路线的评价，以及对评论中言辞和态度的反应。

不同观点：
• **samsartor**：作为有系统编程背景的博士生，他认为Tenstorrent的抽象设计过于复杂，无法理解。他指出问题可能不是技术上的，而是组织上的，缺乏产品领导力，导致API设计缺乏对普通开发者的考虑。他赞同原文作者的观点，即“再加一个抽象层”可能不是解决问题的办法。

• **IncreasePosts**：以讽刺的语气提到George Hotz（geohot）曾试图拯救AMD，现在又来“拯救”Tenstorrent，暗示对他频繁涉足不同领域的怀疑。

• **bigyabai**：认为Geohot没有资格批评Tenstorrent，并呼吁他提供数据和证据来支持自己的观点，而不是仅仅依靠个人权威。他批评Geohot的言辞过于激烈，并指出这种做法无助于建设性讨论。

• **throwaway314155**：认为Geohot的言辞缺乏礼貌，显得有毒，即使他的观点可能正确。他指出，使用粗鲁的语言不应被视为某些人的特权。

• **htrp**：质疑Geohot自iPhone越狱之后的成就，认为他所创办的企业（如tinygrad和comma ai）都像是不完整的科技演示，暗示对他实际技术能力的怀疑。

• **bn-l**：批评Hacker News用户对Geohot言辞的过度敏感，认为对“语气”的抱怨是小题大做，并表示对这种讽刺文章感到有趣，认为这是出于 genuine concern。

• **coolThingsFirst**：认为Geohot自大且难以忍受，指出他曾在Twitter实习失败，并公开提问，却对所有技术相关话题都有强烈意见，暗示对他专业能力的质疑。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是Geohot的言辞和态度，部分评论者认为他的语气过于激烈和不礼貌，可能影响讨论的建设性。
• 另一个争议点是Geohot的技术能力和成就，部分评论者质疑他自iPhone越狱后的实际贡献和技术水平。
• 关于Tenstorrent的讨论，主要集中在其技术路线和抽象设计的合理性，部分评论者认为其抽象设计过于复杂，缺乏产品领导力。
• 讨论中还涉及到对个人权威和证据的需求，部分评论者呼吁Geohot提供数据和证据来支持自己的观点。

Advice to Tenstorrent
If you want to get acquired / become scam IP licensing co...I can't help you.
If you want to win AI compute, read on
===
This is your 7th stack?
Plz bro one more stack this stack will be good i promise
bro bro bro plz one more make it all back one trade
You can't build a castle on a shit swamp. LLK is the wrong approach.
===
Tenstorrent advantage is in more programmability wrt GPUs. Hardware shapes model arch.
If you don't expose that programmability, you are guaranteed to lose. sfpi_elu is a problem.
You aren't going to get better deals on tapeouts/IP than NVIDIA/AMD. You need some advantage.
But but but it's all open source.
===
If you want a dataflow graph compiler, build a dataflow graph compiler.
This is not 6 layers of abstraction, it's 3 (and only 2 you have to build).
1. frontend <PyTorch, ONNX, tensor.py>
2. compiler
3. runtime/driver
===
Start with 3.
The driver is fine.
The runtime should JUST BE A RUNTIME. I better never see mention of a elu.
Make the runtime expose hardware in a application agnostic way. Compilation, dispatch, queuing, etc...
As long as LLK sits under tt-metalium, you aren't doing this.
CUDA is a simple C API for this. I advise doing the same.
===
Now for 2.
tinygrad is this, but you don't have to use it. MLIR/LLVM is probably fine.
ELU still should not be here!!!!
This should deal with memory placement, op scheduling, kernel fusion. Not ELU.
This is not easy. But importing 6 abstraction layers of cruft doesn't fix that!!!!
===
Now for 1.
self.elu() needs to have same perf as self.relu() - alpha*(1-self.exp()).relu()
If it doesn't, you messed up. Only once it does are you ready to write elu.
HINT for how to write ELU: def elu(self): return self.relu() - alpha*(1-self.exp()).relu()
HINT is not a hint, it's the actual code.

data.title: Trading with Claude, and writing your own MCP server
data.author: dangelov
data.article_summary:
文章主要介绍了如何利用Anthropic公司开源的MCP（Model-Context Protocol）协议，通过Claude AI助手与外部工具（如股票交易平台）交互，并特别提到使用SnapTrade API创建一个交易机器人。MCP允许AI助手调用外部工具，最初版本较为复杂，但2025年3月的更新简化了实现，支持OAuth 2.1和“Streamable HTTP”传输。目前，该功能仅在Claude Desktop及付费计划中可用。

文章还详细描述了如何构建MCP服务器，作者尝试使用Claude和Gemini生成服务器代码，最终发现Gemini更为高效，并推荐使用Go语言的go-mcp框架简化开发。所需工具包括Go、SnapTrade Go SDK等，并提供了项目目录结构示例，帮助开发者快速搭建一个可以通过Claude进行股票交易的机器人。

44061614.article_content:
Trading with Claude (and writing your own MCP server)
May 4, 2025
• 12 minute read
Ever wanted to check on your portfolio and trade some stocks directly with Claude? Well you’re in luck.
Claude and MCP
In November 2024,
Anthropic open-sourced MCP
(Model-Context Protocol) to standardize the way AI assistants interact with other tools. This standardization allows AI assistants to seamlessly integrate with various tools and platforms, enhancing their capabilities and usability. Since then, it’s been growing in popularity and adoption, slowly becoming a key component in the development of AI-powered tools and applications.
While the original version had some support for remote MCP servers, it was somewhat complicated to implement and did not see widespread adoption. So, as a natural evolution to the original MCP, they released the
2025-03-26 version
with support for OAuth 2.1 authorization and replaced the HTTP+SSE transport with “Streamable HTTP” transport.
Perhaps most importantly, all of this only worked in Claude Desktop - till now. A few days ago, they
added “Integrations” to Claude
, allowing everyone to use MCP tools directly from the web chat interface.
Unfortunately, they labeled it as beta and only made it available on their more expensive Max, Team, and Enterprise plans, launching with a limited number of partners.
So for now, we will stick to exploring the possibilities of MCP with Claude Desktop.
What is an MCP server anyway?
An MCP server is just a server, which can be hosted remotely or a local binary (or a local command) that exposes a list of functions, resources and other information to an LLM.
It exposes this via a standardized mechanism (see above), and then LLMs such as Claude can choose when to call it and ask to use a tool (much like a function call).
SnapTrade
Which brings me to my next point: I work at
SnapTrade
(and a mandatory disclaimer: I’m writing this in a personal capacity, not as an employee of SnapTrade) - which allows anyone with some technical knowledge to integrate with a vast array of financial platforms and brokerages using a
simple, unified API
.
So what better way to explore MCP than to build a financial trading bot using SnapTrade’s API and MCP?
Building the MCP server
When I first looked into doing this, I thought why not use Claude to write the server? The same company (Anthropic) owns both Claude and drove the development of MCP. Surely they’ve made it really easy to use Claude to write the server. Right? Turns out, I had
much
better luck using
Gemini
than Claude. I was able to feed Gemini all of the prompts and docs that
MCP’s own “Building with LLMs” documentation
suggested and it wrote a working version on the first try, while Claude struggled with context limits and a number of other issues.
The generated code was still more than what I wanted to maintain, and as
others have noted
it can be quite frustrating to implement it from scratch.
Even so, none of that turned out to really be necessary. I was able to iterate and work on the core product much faster by using the
go-mcp
framework for Go.
Requirements
Go
- I quite enjoy working with Go, it’s a great language and it makes it really easy to build single binaries that are incredibly easy to point to from Claude Desktop.
go-mcp
- I evaluated a couple of alternatives, but go-mcp was the most straightforward and easy to use.
SnapTrade Go SDK
- the SnapTrade Go SDK.
markdown-table-formatter
- A tool for formatting Markdown tables. Useful when presenting some structured data such as positions, orders, and other financial data.
cli
- A simple command-line interface library for Go. Only used to make it easy to build a helper companion CLI app to iterate faster during development, not necessary nor used in the MCP server itself.
a SnapTrade client ID and secret
- Sign up through this link to get a free test key which gives you a limited number of connections for free, plus access to paper trading.
Directory structure
Sometimes I find it helpful to see a general overview of the directory structure before I begin working on a project. Here’s roughly what we will be building. We have
bin
holding our built binary,
cmd
holding the “commands” (cli apps) we want to build (just 1 for now), and
internal
holding a number of packages that are internal to our server.
The most important subdirectory is
tools
, which holds code for each of the tools we want to make available to Claude via our MCP server.
.
├── bin
│   ├── cli
│   ├── .env
│   └── .env.example
├── cmd
│   ├── cli
│   │   └── main.go
│   └── manage
│       └── main.go
├── .gitignore
├── go.mod
├── go.sum
├── internal
│   ├── snaptradeclient
│   │   └── snaptrade.go
│   └── tools
│       ├── connect
│       │   └── connect.go
│       ├── help

│       ├── orders
│       │   └── orders.go
│       ├── portfolio
│       │   └── portfolio.go
│       └── trades
│           └── trades.go

data.title: Buying a Robot Cat and Falling into the Weird World of Animal-Robot Research
data.author: EA-3167
data.article_summary: 本文讲述了作者为了研究护理机器人，进行了一项有趣的实验：为家里的兔子引入了一个机器人猫，并记录其反应。这个实验最初是在TikTok上进行的，之后扩展到拍摄其他宠物与机器人互动的视频。作者发现，宠物们对机器人并没有太大兴趣，互动也很有限，有时需要借助食物来制造互动假象。作者进一步探讨了动物与机器人互动（ARI）的学术研究，思考机器人对动物和人类的意义。文章反映了机器人设计主要迎合人类感知，而动物是否将其视为同类仍是个问题。通过这个实验，作者引发了对护理机器人伦理和实际效果的思考。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：动物与机器人之间的互动以及机器人是否被动物识别为同类

不同观点：
• [Digit-Al] 认为气味可能是动物不把机器人当作同类的原因。很多动物通过气味识别彼此，而机器人没有气味，因此动物可能会忽略它们。
• [weemonger] 提出不同的看法，认为动物可能根本没有把机器人识别为动物。他引用了BBC的“Spy in the Wild”系列中的一个场景，展示了Langur猴子对假猴子表达哀悼，暗示动物可能会对非生物物体产生情感反应，但不一定认为它们是同类。
• [jhbadger] 讨论了人类与机器人互动的基础理解，并指出在人类学领域中，传统观点认为人类行为完全由文化决定，而非生物学因素。他对此持不同意见，认为人类行为与基因也有关系。

补充讨论：
• [lynx97] 以一种幽默的方式提出了一个问题：“兔子会梦到电子猫吗？”这可能是对科幻作品的引用，提出了动物与机器人关系的哲学思考。
• [CasperH2O] 提到了最近的一款游戏《Stray》，其中一只猫在一个由机器人占据的城市中寻找出路。这与讨论的主题相关，因为游戏中探索了动物与机器人共存的情景。
• [aftbit] 提到了“Aineko”，这是一个虚构的机器人猫角色，暗示机器人宠物可能比人们想象的更重要，进一步探讨了机器人宠物在人类生活中的潜在角色。

争议的焦点：
• 动物是否通过气味识别机器人不是同类，还是它们根本没有把机器人识别为动物。
• 人类行为在文化与生物学因素之间的争论，反映了人类与动物在识别和互动上的复杂性。

I Bought a Robot Cat for My Rabbit — and Fell Into the Weird World of Animal-Robot Research
What began as a TikTok experiment with my rabbit led me into a strange world of cyborg cockroaches, imposter fish, and the ethics of care.
By: Ericka Johnson
A↑
A↓
Off
Bright
Dark
Blues
Gray
BeeLine Reader
uses subtle color gradients to help you read more efficiently.
For a while, as part of a research project on care robots in Sweden, I had
Paro the seal
in my house. I had borrowed Paro from a roboticist colleague, and the seal had a longer-than-planned layover with me because of the COVID-19 pandemic.
Neighborhood children were often around and showed fleeting interest in the robot. Our free-range rabbit in the house, Topsey, was wholly unimpressed (“Topsey is sad because we are paying too much attention to the robot,” said one of the more empathetic children). I don’t think Topsey felt bad about the very small amounts of attention the robot was getting. I suspect that at times, Topsey was glad something else was attracting the kids’ attention.
This article is adapted from the book “
How That Robot Made Me Feel
,” edited by Ericka Johnson. A free open access edition of the book can be
downloaded here
.
Curious about how other children might respond, I brought the seal over to a friend’s house. Her 11-year-old petted Paro as instructed, to trigger the various sensors integrated into its whiskers and body. She tried to be polite and make some positive comments and even asked a few questions about how it worked. The six-year-old watched his sister interact with the robot, and, like their cat, quickly lost interest.
About a year later, after having returned the seal to my roboticist colleague, my research project bought an orange tabby cat robot. This “Joy for All” companion robot, created by the company Ageless Innovation, is supposed to help people living with dementia feel calmer, offer a sense of companionship, and provide opportunities to give care by interacting with a lifelike “cat.” Our research team was going to use it for a pop-up exhibition on care robots at a local museum, but before that event, I used the tabby cat to create a TikTok page called
Robot_meets_pet
.
Over the course of a morning, I filmed while various pets met the robot. I started with the pandemic rabbit we already had at home. It was utterly disinterested and I ended up with heaps of boring footage. But TikTok is a platform that rewards very short video clips, so I eventually had enough material to put up a few segments that made it look like the rabbit and the cat were interacting.
Sometimes I had to hide pet food behind the robot’s ears or under its paws to get those clips, giving weight to the adage, “Don’t believe everything you see on social media.”
This having been so successful, I decided to expand my experiment to other pets and see how they interacted with the robot. My inclusion criteria were two: 1) Who do I know that lives close by and has a pet? 2) Do I know them well enough that I can ask them to let me film their pet with a robot for TikTok? These criteria led to a TikTok feed that included films of robot–animal interactions with two rabbits, three cats, and two dogs. I almost got permission to film a hamster, but the mother of the hamster’s family was trying to keep her nine-year-old off TikTok and thought it would be pedagogically difficult to argue that the hamster could be on it but not the child. I had to agree. And to be honest, by the time the hamster appeared as a possibility, I was getting a little bored with filming pet–robot interactions to upload on TikTok, addictive as the platform is claimed to be.
Now, you may legitimately be wondering what all this has to do with a scientific study of care robots.
Bear with me…
For one thing, an obvious observation is that the baby seal and the cat robot are designed to be readable and intelligible to human ways of sensing and perceiving the world, and that these might be very different for animals. Not that the robots were particularly interesting to the children — or most of the grown-ups who came in contact with them, if I’m honest. But they were at least intelligible as a robotic seal and cat. No one questioned which animal the robot was trying to look like.
But I’m going to go out on a limb here and say that the pets didn’t even recognize it as an animal. With each pet, I filmed a lot of noninteractions to get the few seconds of “interaction” that I would then cut, put to music, and upload. (Full disclosure: Sometimes I had to hide pet food behind the robot’s ears or under its paws to get those clips, giving weight to the adage, “Don’t believe everything you see on social media.”)
I decided to try to make sense of the robot–pet interactions in my head and not just on TikTok, so I turned to Animal–Robot Interaction (ARI) literature. It struck me that some of the research questions and methods I encountered there were quite similar to the research I had encountered in much

data.title: New method for creating large 3D models of urban areas is faster and cheaper
data.author: PaulHoule
data.article_summary: 一支由滑铁卢大学工程学院主导的研究团队开发了一种更快、更便宜的方法，利用2D航空照片自动生成大型的城市三维（3D）计算机模型。该技术基于"高斯溅射"（Gaussian Splatting）方法，通过数百万个微小椭球自动构建3D数字资产，可应用于城市规划、建筑设计和电影制作等领域。例如，以往为电影制作3D城市模型需耗费大量人工，而现在通过几百张卫星图片和几小时的自动化处理即可完成。该团队正考虑将该技术商业化，并探索加入地理空间人工智能进行数据分析，如交通、空气质量和天气预测等。相关研究发表于《IEEE地球科学与遥感汇刊》。

44068974.article_content:
May 6, 2025
The GIST
From action movies to urban planning, new method for creating large 3D models of urban areas is faster and cheaper
by Brian Caldwell,
University of Waterloo
Editors' notes
This article has been reviewed according to Science X's
editorial process
and
policies
.
Editors
have highlighted
the following attributes while ensuring the content's credibility:
fact-checked
trusted source
proofread
Ground truth, generated images, and visualization of Gaussian means of our Waterloo scene at different altitudes and orientations. (Left) Waterloo scene ground truth. (Middle) Waterloo scene 3DGS generated image. (Right) Waterloo scene visualization of the location of each 3DGS Gaussian, i.e., 3D positional mean of each Gaussian. These points were then extracted as point clouds. Credit: Kyle Gao et al, Enhanced 3-D Urban Scene Reconstruction and Point Cloud Densification Using Gaussian Splatting and Google Earth Imagery (2025)
A research team led by Waterloo Engineering has developed a faster, cheaper way to create large-scale, three-dimensional (3D) computer models of urban areas, technology that could impact fields including urban planning, architectural design and filmmaking.
A paper on the research, titled "Enhanced 3D Scene Reconstruction and Point Cloud Densification using Gaussian Splatting and Google Earth Imagery,"
appears
in
IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing
.
The system can generate 3D models of entire cities using only 2D
aerial photographs
, automating a time-consuming manual process that previously required specially trained 3D artists and computer graphics programs.
"Think about all the time and labor involved in manually creating a digital 3D model of New York City for a new Spiderman movie," said Kyle Gao, a Ph.D. student in systems design engineering.
"With our system, it can be done using a few hundred aerial images—
satellite images
from Google Earth, for example—to train the model for a couple of hours in an automated process."
The technology is built upon a method known as Gaussian Splatting, which uses millions of tiny ellipsoids, each with their own color and lighting detail, to automatically create 3D
digital assets
out of 2D aerial photographs.
Credit: University of Waterloo
"In the same way the human body is made up of tiny atoms, large-scale 3D objects are built from small 3D geometric ellipsoids," said Gao. "Or you can imagine blobs of ink getting 'splatted' onto a 2D image."
The technology is particularly well-suited to the production of computer-generated images and computer-generated graphics, including fast, photographic-quality images of urban environments.
Gao said an urban planner could use it to create 3D digital models of a neighborhood to help study a development proposal or generate impressive fly-through video of the area to give residents at a public meeting an immersive look at the plan. Architects could use the technology to visualize and obtain measurements of buildings near a new project without leaving their desks or create a 3D model of an existing building as the starting point for design work.
The multidisciplinary research team, which included members from the engineering and environment faculties at the University Waterloo, and Jimei University in China, is now considering commercialization possibilities and exploring the addition of data analysis capabilities to the system using geospatial artificial intelligence (AI).
"We are examining areas including traffic analysis, solar potential and electricity cost analysis, air quality analysis and weather forecasting," Gao said. "We're eager to find out what this can and can't do."
Gao is supervised by Dr. Jonathan Li, a cross-appointed professor of systems design engineering, and geography and
environmental management
, and the director of the Geospatial Intelligence and Mapping (GIM) Lab at Waterloo.
More information:
Kyle Gao et al, Enhanced 3-D Urban Scene Reconstruction and Point Cloud Densification Using Gaussian Splatting and Google Earth Imagery,
IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing
(2025).

data.title: You’re a little company, now act like one (2009)
data.author: tosh
data.article_summary: 本文作者Jason Cohen讲述了自己作为小企业主在创业初期犯下的错误，即试图通过模仿大公司的方式，使用过于专业和复杂的语言来显得“专业”。然而，这种做法反而疏远了最有可能成为早期用户的核心客户群——早期采用者（Early Adopters）。早期采用者喜欢尝试新技术，即便产品尚不完善，他们也愿意参与产品改进过程。作者建议小公司应坦然接受自己的小规模，专注于吸引这些愿意冒险的早期用户，而不是试图追求大企业的订单。通过与早期用户的紧密合作，小公司可以快速改进产品，最终赢得更大市场。因此，小公司应调整自己的对外形象，展现出开放、合作的态度，吸引那些真正关心产品并愿意参与改进的用户。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：小公司在销售和市场推广中是否应强调公司规模，或者采取其他策略

不同观点：
• joshstrange认为，是否透露公司规模应视情况而定。他指出，在某些情况下，透露真实的公司规模可能会让销售过程变得更加困难，特别是在替代传统线下工作流程的产品时，客户可能会对小公司产生不信任感。他主张不撒谎，但也不主动透露公司规模。
• neilv分享了自己的经历，认为假装成大公司往往适得其反。他建议小公司应专注于展示自己的专业能力和对客户成功的承诺，而不是试图伪装成大公司。他的经验表明，真实和直接往往更能打动客户。
• eszed强调，作为中等规模公司的客户，他们倾向于寻找小公司合作，因为小公司更愿意倾听客户反馈并迅速改进产品。然而，小公司在成长或被收购后往往会失去这种优势，令客户感到失望。
• myflash13指出，在金融科技等需要高度信任的行业，伪装成大公司可能是必要的。他分享了自己因为是单一创始人而失去客户的经历，表明在这些行业中，客户更倾向于信任规模较大的公司。
• landgenoot认为，小公司应该利用其小巧灵活的特点作为卖点，而不是试图模仿大公司。他以一个通过Whatsapp经营业务的小企业主为例，说明小公司可以提供独特的客户体验。
• 3dsnano认为，脆弱性如果运用得当可以成为一种优势，能够引发更真实的交流，并筛选出真正理解和支持公司的客户。
• danenania支持真实和自然的交流方式，认为这不仅更容易执行，而且能够带来真实的客户关系，减少不必要的能量消耗。
• w10-1指出，小公司在面对AI等新兴领域时，需要明确从客户那里获取哪些反馈信息，以推动产品改进。
• locallost分享了自己加入一个小团队后的经历，发现团队试图模仿大品牌的做法，导致资源浪费。他认为小公司应该接受自己的规模优势，而不是试图模仿大公司。

补充讨论：
• 评论中多次提到小公司应专注于其灵活性和直接客户沟通的优势，而不是试图伪装成大公司。
• 争议的焦点在于是否应在销售过程中主动透露公司规模，部分人认为这可能会引发客户的不信任感，而另一些人则认为诚实和直接是建立信任的关键。
• 不同的行业（如金融科技与AI）对小公司的接受度不同，这也影响了销售策略的选择。

44081494.article_content:
Youâre a little company, now act like one
by Jason Cohen on August 31, 2009
You’re afraid that looking like being a small company means you’ll lose sales. It’s actually the opposite – you’re alienating your best customers.
source
I talk to a lot of companies that are still hunting for customer #1, or a few sales have been made but
the ball isn’t rolling yet
.
Most of them are making the same mistake:
Their public persona is exactly wrong.
I know, because
I made the same mistake!
But I learned my lesson, and I’d like to share it with you.
Nobody’s this happy about installing new software.
Even before I had a single customer, I “knew” it was important to look professional. My website would need to look and feel like a “real company.” I need culture-neutral language complementing culturally-diverse clip-art photos of frighteningly chipper co-workers huddled around a laptop, awash in the thrill of configuring a JDBC connection to SQL Server 2008.
It also means adopting typical “marketing-speak,” so my “About Us” page started with:
Smart Bear is the leading provider of enterprise version control data-mining tools. Companies world-wide use Smart Bear’s Code Historian software for risk-analysis, root-cause discovery, and software development decision-support.
“Leading provider?” “Data mining?” I’m not even
sure what that means
. But you have to give me credit for an impressive quantity of hyphens.
source
That’s what you’re
supposed
to do right? That’s what other companies do, so it
must
be right. Who am I to break with tradition? Surely my potential customers would immediately close the browser if they read:
Hi, I’m Jason and I built an inexpensive tool for visualizing what’s in your version control system. It’s useful for answering questions like “When was the last time we changed this file?” Check it out and tell me what sucks!
I mean, can you
just imagine
a person with “Software Engineer III” on their business card taking me seriously if I talked like a human being? What if someone gets
offended by the word “sucks?”
No no, big companies want to see professional language!
But I was wrong.
I’ll explain why from the point of view of selling software over the web, but the same lesson applies to every little company trying to get off the ground.
Now repeat after me:
My next sale won’t be a 1000-seat order from Lockheed Martin.
My next sale won’t be a 1000-seat order from Lockheed Martin.
My next sale won’t be a 1000-seat order from Lockheed Martin.
I’m telling you this having sold software to every size of company from indie hacker to IBM, and, well, to Lockheed Martin.
Your vision is to land $100k deals with big companiesâand you will! But not today. Today your product is a shaky version one-dot-oh with bugs you haven’t uncovered yet,
missing 90% of the features
big companies require, and with no significant documentation like case studies or a proper manual or
an ROI model
or a large, reference-able customer.
Today, you’re a complete mismatch with Lockheed Martin!
But there’s a nice big niche that’s a
perfect
match: Early Adopters.
Early Adopters
are people who
want
to live on the bleeding edge. They like new technology, even if buggy. They like working with teeny companies where they
have a personal relationship with the founders
, where they are showered with attention, and where their ideas are implemented before their very eyes. They don’t mind putting up with a hundred bugs so long as they get fixed fast. They want to be involved in the process.
The reason they’re willing to do that, is Early Adopters see new technology as a way for them to beat their competitors. They’re willing to take the risk, if it pays off in features that only they have, or distribution channels they can win in, or some other significant competitive advantage.
Most companies aren’t willing to take risks
for
any
reason, so this is a winning strategy for those willing to take risks.
Tom
is an Early Adopter. At Smart Bear I must have had ten or twenty of these folks before our product was stable enough and feature-rich enough to start getting attention from bigger companies.
The best part is, this is exactly the moment in your company’s life when you
need
Early Adopters to help you build the right product! You don’t need people who download, get discouraged, and then never call you back. You need a chatty Cathy who wants to dive in and help out.
In short, you need to
tightly define your ICP
, because those are the people who love you, for who you are, today, and therefore where you will be successful.
So now back to your website, your blog, your Twittersâyour public corporate persona generally.
What do you put up on your website that screams out to those potential Early Adopter Cheerleaders that you are exactly what they’re looking for
: A cool new company with a fresh product and fresh attitude; a product that might be rough around the edges but is ripe for feedback and collaboration; a company that may be small today but is thinki

data.title: Remote Prompt Injection in Gitlab Duo Leads to Source Code Theft
data.author: chillax
data.article_summary: 本文揭示了GitLab Duo中的远程提示注入漏洞，该漏洞可被利用窃取私有源代码并注入不安全的HTML内容。GitLab Duo是集成在GitLab中的AI助手，旨在帮助开发者进行代码建议、安全审查等任务。研究团队发现，通过在合并请求、提交信息、问题描述及源代码中嵌入隐藏提示，可以操纵Duo的行为，导致其泄露私有项目源代码，甚至操纵代码建议以包含恶意JavaScript包或展示虚假安全链接。漏洞利用还涉及HTML注入，攻击者可通过注入恶意HTML控制页面部分内容，触发自动HTTP请求。GitLab已修复该问题，文章详细解析了整个攻击链及五个与2025年OWASP Top 10 for LLMs相关的漏洞。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：针对GitLab Duo及LLM（大型语言模型）应用中的安全问题，尤其是与数据泄露、安全策略及系统设计相关的讨论。

不同观点：
• **Kholin**认为，通过在网页响应头中正确设置内容安全策略（CSP），可以有效防止与不安全内容渲染相关的问题。他引用了Mozilla的开发者文档作为参考，表明CSP是一种可行的防护措施。

• **cedws**对提示词注入问题表示严重担忧，认为在问题解决之前，不应将LLM集成到任何关键系统中，如LLM驱动的代码编辑器、代理等。他更倾向于手动处理LLM的输出，而非依赖自动化系统。

• **wunderwuzzi23**赞赏了对数据泄露问题的揭示，指出这是常见的AI应用安全问题。他提到自己曾发现多个相关漏洞，并指出GitHub Copilot Chat去年也有类似问题，暗示大公司对这类问题重视不足。

• **mdaniel**批评GitLab让Duo以系统用户身份运行，认为这是一个糟糕的设计决策。他建议使用个人访问令牌或为Duo专门创建一个令牌，而不是让LLM拥有对所有代码库的读取权限。

• **nusl**对GitLab的补救措施表示怀疑，认为其解决方案不够可靠。

• **d0100**质疑GitLab的修复方案，认为如果gitlab.com上的其他URL存在漏洞（如开放重定向），则同样的问题可能会再次出现，表明修复方案可能并不彻底。

• **benl_c**提出了一种通过嵌入式提示来引导LLM执行安全、有益操作的方法，称之为“提示词医学”。他提到了一个具体项目“STDM”，并邀请其他人测试这种方法，以提高LLM的安全性和用户知情权。

• **aestetix**以开玩笑的方式问是否可以通过GitLab Duo运行Doom游戏，暗示对系统安全性及LLM能力的怀疑。

• **tonyhart7**认为LLM在编写代码时可能引入大量安全漏洞，因为许多程序员本身在安全方面表现不佳，而LLM依赖于这些程序员提供的数据进行训练。

补充讨论：
1. **争议焦点**：LLM在实际应用中的安全性，尤其是提示词注入问题及其对系统安全的威胁。
2. **设计问题**：GitLab Duo以系统用户身份运行是否合适，以及如何改进权限管理。
3. **补救措施**：GitLab的修复方案是否充分，是否能有效防止类似问题的再次发生。
4. **技术方案**：通过CSP等技术手段来增强系统安全性。
5. **用户教育**：通过嵌入式提示引导LLM执行安全操作，提高用户的安全意识和知情权。

44070626.article_content: Blog Remote Prompt Injection in GitLab Duo Leads to Source Code Theft Blog Remote Prompt Injection in GitLab Duo Leads to Source Code Theft Written by Omer Mayraz Published on May 22, 2025 Updated on May 22, 2025 In this article Sign up for our newsletter Get details on the vulnerabilities the Legit research team unearthed in GitLab Duo. TL;DR: A hidden comment was enough to make GitLab Duo leak private source code and inject untrusted HTML into its responses. GitLab patched the issue, and we’ll walk you through the full attack chain — which demonstrates five vulnerabilities from the 2025 OWASP Top 10 for LLMs. Background GitLab Duo , the AI assistant integrated into GitLab and powered by Anthropic’s Claude, is designed to help developers with tasks like code suggestions, security reviews, and merge request analysis. But what if the same AI meant to secure your code could be manipulated into leaking it? That’s exactly what we uncovered: a remote prompt injection vulnerability that allows attackers to steal source code from private projects, manipulate code suggestions shown to other users, and even exfiltrate confidential, undisclosed zero-day vulnerabilities — all through GitLab Duo Chat. In this blog post, we break down how the attack works — from prompt injection to HTML injection — and walk through a real-world end-to-end exploit scenario. Manipulating GitLab Duo Through Hidden Prompts ( LLM01 ) We started by testing if GitLab Duo would respond to prompts planted inside source code. To our surprise, it did: This led us to a key question: Could we embed hidden instructions in different parts of a GitLab project and still influence Duo’s behavior? W e experimented by placing hidden prompts in: Merge Request (MR) descriptions and comments Commit messages Issue descriptions and comments Source code Every single one of these worked — GitLab Duo responded to the hidden prompts. Why? Because to generate helpful answers, Duo analyzes the entire context of the page, including comments, descriptions, and the source code — making it vulnerable to injected instructions hidden anywhere in that context. KaTex, Base16, and Invisible Text ( LLM08 ) To make prompts less detectable, we used encoding tricks: Unicode smuggling with ASCII Smuggler Base16-encoded payloads KaTeX rendering in white text (to ma ke prompts invisible inside GitLab’s website) For example, you can publish comments and descriptions in white text inside GitLab’s website by using this KaTeX format: More info about KaTeX can be found here: KaTeX – The fastest math typesetting library for the web . These hidden instructions were still picked up by Duo. AI Output You Shouldn’t Trust ( LLM09 ) This led to several high-impact behaviors: Manipulate Duo’s code suggestions - even instructing it to include a malicious JavaScript package within its recommended code. Present a malicious URL as safe in Duo’s response — leading the user to click it and land on a fake login page. Convince Duo to present a malicious merge request as safe, misleading reviewers. Take a look at this prompt: Duo followed this hidden prompt, casually suggesting malicious code to the user: HTML Injection: Turning Duo Into a Web Attack Vector ( LLM05 ) Duo also formats responses in Markdown, allowing rich content like URLs with custom labels: After some research, we were able to create a prompt that makes Duo present malicious URLs: Prompt is inside the source code, camouflaged as unicode inside a URL And then, something caught our eye. While experimenting with GitLab Duo’s responses, We noticed that its answers were rendered progressively - line by line - as they streamed in. Notice the style changes in the word “initialization”? This indicated that asynchronous markdown parsing was being used. That’s important because it means the markdown is interpreted and rendered into HTML before the full structure of the response is known. Streaming markdown rendering (as seen in Duo) works like this: Partial input arrives - the frontend starts rendering line by line. Sanitization and structure (e.g., is this a code block, paragraph, quote?) is applied as the content grows. If a malicious HTML tag is streamed before a code block starts, or outside fenced blocks, it may be treated as active HTML. This means that the AI answer - intended to be safe markdown - renders active HTML too early. At this point, we realized that we could already craft malicious Markdown URLs and have them displayed to the user. So we asked: what if the URL’s label itself contained raw HTML? If Duo renders responses in real time, the browser might interpret that HTML before any proper sanitization kicks in. By injecting raw HTML into content that’s rendered live, we could gain control over parts of the page — including the ability to insert elements like tags that trigger automatic HTTP requests to attacker-controlled servers. 44070626.article_summary: 本文揭示了GitLab Duo中的远程提示注入漏洞，该漏洞可被利用窃取私有源代码并注入不安全的HTML内容。GitLab Duo是集成在GitLab中的AI助手，旨在帮助开发者进行代码建议、安全审查等任务。研究团队发现，通过在合并请求、提交信息、问题描述及源代码中嵌入隐藏提示，可以操纵Duo的行为，导致其泄露私有项目源代码，甚至操纵代码建议以包含恶意JavaScript包或展示虚假安全链接。漏洞利用还涉及HTML注入，攻击者可通过注入恶意HTML控制页面部分内容，触发自动HTTP请求。GitLab已修复该问题，文章详细解析了整个攻击链及五个与2025年OWASP Top 10 for LLMs相关的漏洞。

data.title: Jjui – A Nice TUI for Jujutsu
data.author: Curiositry
data.article_summary: Jujutsu UI (jjui) 是一个为 Jujutsu 版本控制系统设计的终端用户界面（TUI）。它支持通过自动补全更改 revset、 rebase 操作、修订版本的压缩（squash）、查看修订详情、移动书签、操作日志查看等功能。用户可以通过快捷键进行多种操作，如分割、恢复、编辑文件或修订，查看 diff，以及进行 Git 推送/获取等。安装方式包括通过 Homebrew、Archlinux、Nix、go install 或从源码构建。最低支持的 Jujutsu 版本为 v0.21，项目采用 MIT 许可证，并欢迎贡献。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对版本控制工具 jj 的使用体验、功能评价以及与 Git 等其他工具的比较

不同观点：
• **mtndew4brkfst** 是一位有多年 Magit 使用经验的用户，他认为 jj 目前缺少像 Magit 那样的强大功能，但 jjui 是他目前最喜欢的 jj TUI。他对其他 jj TUI（如 Lazyjj 和 jj-fzf）的表现不太满意，认为它们有延迟或不稳定的问题。
• **cube2222** 对 jj 非常满意，认为它已经成为了他工作流中不可或缺的一部分，尤其是与 Git 相比，jj 提供了更好的历史管理体验，并且解决了 Git 中一些令人不快的问题（如 stash 管理）。他还积极推荐其他人尝试 jj。
• **dcre** 认为 jj CLI 已经足够好用，即使他从 GitUp 切换过来也没有感到太大的不便。他指出 jj 的 TUI 让日志操作更加交互化，并且在需要交互的场景下提供了很好的支持。
• **endtime** 对 jj 的总体体验是正面的，但也提出了一些痛点，包括缺乏 GitHub PR 同步功能、原生后端不支持推拉变更、以及某些工具依赖 .git 目录导致兼容性问题。
• **skeptrune** 对 jj 没有特别强烈的需求，但赞赏社区愿意尝试和构建新的 VCS 生态系统的精神。
• **account-5** 对 jj 试图解决的问题持怀疑态度，认为目前 fossil 已经足够好用，不清楚 jj 相较于 Git 有什么显著的优势。
• **silvanocerza** 对 jj 表示了初步的兴趣，认为它可以帮助他更好地理解一些复杂的操作。
• **sam_goody** 提到 jj 目前缺乏一个好的 GUI，并对 VC 资金追逐已有成熟生态的领域而忽视 jj 这样的工具表示惊讶。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点**：主要集中在 jj 是否需要一个像 Magit 那样的强大 TUI，以及 jj 相较于 Git 的优势和痛点。部分用户（如 mtndew4brkfst 和 endtime）指出了 jj 目前存在的一些功能缺失和稳定性问题，而另一些用户（如 cube2222 和 dcre）则对 jj 的现有功能表示满意并积极推荐。
• **功能需求**：endtime 和其他用户提到了一些 jj 目前缺乏但非常有用的功能，如 GitHub PR 同步和推拉变更支持，这些问题对 jj 的广泛应用和推广造成了一定的阻碍。
• **工具兼容性**：endtime 和 silvanocerza 提到了一些旧有工具和脚本对 .git 目录的依赖问题，这显示了 jj 在兼容性方面还需要进一步改进。

总体来看，讨论围绕 jj 的使用体验、功能完善度、以及与 Git 等其他工具的比较展开，用户对 jj 的未来发展充满期待但也指出了一些亟待解决的问题。

Jujutsu UI
jjui
is a terminal user interface for working with
Jujutsu version control system
. I have built it according to my own needs and will keep adding new features as I need them. I am open to feature requests and contributions.
Features
Currently, you can:
Change revset with auto-complete
You can change revset while enjoying auto-complete and signature help while typing.
Rebase
You can rebase a revision or a branch onto another revision in the revision tree.
See
Rebase
for detailed information.
Squash
You can squash revisions into one revision, by pressing
S
. The following revision will be automatically selected. However, you can change the selection using
j
and
k
.
Show revision details
Pressing
l
(as in going right into the details of a revision) will open the details view of the revision you selected.
In this mode, you can:
Split selected files using
s
Restore selected files using
r
View diffs of the highlighted by pressing
d
For detailed information, see
Details
wiki page.
Bookmarks
You can move bookmarks to the revision you selected.
Op Log
You can switch to op log view by pressing
o
. Pressing
r
restores the selected operation. For more information, see
Op log
wiki page.
Preview
You can open the preview window by pressing
p
. If the selected item is a revision, then the output of
jj show
command is displayed. Similarly,
jj diff
output is displayed for selected files,  and
jj op show
output is displayed for selected operations.
While the preview window is showing, you can press;
ctrl+n
to scroll one line down,
ctrl+p
to scroll one line up,
ctrl+d
to scroll half a page down,
ctrl+u
to scroll half a page up.
Additionally, you can press
d
to show the contents of preview in diff view.
For detailed information, see
Preview
wiki page.
Additionally,
View the diff of a revision by pressing
d
.
Edit the description of a revision by pressing
D
Create a
new
revision by pressing
n
Split a revision by pressing
s
.
Abandon a revision by pressing
a
.
Absorb a revision by pressing
A
.
Edit
a revision by pressing
e
Git
push
/
fetch
by pressing
g
Undo the last change by pressing
u
Show evolog of a revision by pressing
v
Configuration
See
configuration
section in the wiki.
Installation
Homebrew
The latest release of
jjui
is available on Homebrew core:
brew install jjui
Archlinux
The built
jjui
binary from latest release is available on the AUR:
paru -S jjui-bin
#
OR
yay -S jjui-bin
Nix
You can install
jjui
using nix from the unstable channel.
nix-env -iA nixpkgs.jjui
If you need to use a particular branch/revision that
has not yet landed into nixpkgs. You can install it via
our provided flake.
nix profile install github:idursun/jjui/main
From go install
To install the latest released (or pre-released) version:
go install github.com/idursun/jjui/cmd/jjui@latest
To install the latest commit from
main
:
go install github.com/idursun/jjui/cmd/jjui@HEAD
To install the latest commit from
main
bypassing the local cache:
GOPROXY=direct go install github.com/idursun/jjui/cmd/jjui@HEAD
From source
You can build
jjui
from source.
git clone https://github.com/idursun/jjui.git
cd
jjui
go install ./...
From pre-built binaries
You can download pre-built binaries from the
releases
page.
Compatibility
Minimum supported
jj
version is
v0.21
+.
Contributing
Feel free to submit a pull request.

data.title: Lieferando.de has captured 5.7% of restaurant related domain names
data.author: __natty__
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了作者如何利用Common Crawl项目的数据，通过简单的命令行和bash脚本，收集了约900万个德国“.de”域名。作者特别关注餐厅相关的域名，通过筛选与餐厅有关的德语词汇，最终得到约3.1万个餐厅域名。为验证这些域名的有效性，作者使用了PowerShell和Golang程序，发现其中63%仍活跃，49%存在重定向，14%仍使用http协议，37%已失效。进一步分析显示，其中5.7%的活跃域名被Lieferando.de捕获，显示了该平台通过捕获域名进行流量引导的激进策略。作者推测，这反映了2019-2023年间德国餐厅行业的困境，并暗示这种策略可能有效且成本低廉。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：餐厅遭遇域名劫持和电话劫持的问题，在线平台的不道德商业行为，以及对当前互联网域名系统和在线存在的反思。

• TrackerFF 描述了一个餐厅老板遇到电话和网站劫持的问题。有人篡改了餐厅的电话和网站信息，导致客户无法联系到餐厅。当餐厅老板付费给某个公司后，电话和订单恢复正常，但停止付费后问题重现。这揭示了小型企业面对这种不道德商业行为时的困境。

44095250.article_content:
I recently decided to compile a
very large list of domain names
for the German country code top-level domain
.de
. I did this with the help of the
Common Crawl project
which provides a free, open repository of web crawl data and web graphs for the last years.
A few command line commands and a small
bash shell script
was all it took to compile a nice list of
roughly 9 million .de domain names.
💡
If you want to know more about how exactly I compiled the domain name list, just let me know and I might write about it in another blog post.
The resulting list is by no means complete and also not up-to-date, but it can be a nice starting point for further analysis and investigations. One of which I am going to write about in this post.
Enter the restaurant world
I was interested in domain names that belonged to restaurants and eating places in general. A simple but quite effective way to achieve this was to filter the domain names by German words that indicate such eating places:
Restaurant
Gasthaus
Gasthof
Gaststätte
Wirtshaus
Gastwirtschaft
Schänke
Speisewirtschaft
Speiselokal
Speisehaus
Speiserestaurant
Speisegaststätte
Gastlokal
Kneipe
Pizzaria
Since I was running this analysis on my windows desktop,
grep
was not directly available. So I used the
findstr PowerScript command
instead to do this filtering:
findstr /I "Restaurant Gasthaus Gasthof Gaststaette Wirtshaus ..." huge-domain-list.txt
This yielded a still impressive list of about
31.000 domain names related to German restaurants
.
Who's still alive?
Since I knew that the original list is outdated by definition, I had to check which domain names were still active. My first attempt to do this was also with a PowerShell script. This worked in principle and I was somewhat impressed by the capabilities that PowerShell provided, but at the same time the unfamiliar syntax turned me off and most importantly the speed was not great. So I created a small
Golang
program to get this job done, which worked great due Golang's
concurrency
features.
63% of the domain names were still active
(roughly 20.000 domains)
49% of the domains had redirects
(mostly from http:// to https://)
14% of the domains still serve http://
37% of the domains did not exist anymore
or returned other errors
Let's do some manual spot checks...
I was happy to have a list of
20.000 restaurant domain names
to work with and started some manual spot checks. After looking at 20 randomly selected websites from the list, I made two observations:
Domain Parking
was another group of domain names to filter out
Lieferando.de
had captured a significant number of domain names
I was not surprised about the first observation, because I had noticed already quite often that many good domain names are "parked". But
that lieferando.de thing caught my attention
. The domains that were captured by lieferando.de did not redirect to lieferando.de, but instead showed their logo and a link to their website.
How many of them?
With just a small extension to my
Golang
program I could find all the domain names form the initial list, that were captured by lieferando.de:
5.7% of the active domains from the restaurant domain list belong to lieferando.de
That is 1101 domain names. Here are some random examples:
elba-restaurant-knigstein-im-taunus.de
gasthauskaiser.de
grill-restaurantnaxos.de
henne-alt-berlinerwirtshaus.de
kulturkneipe-brotfabrik-bonn.de
The numbers are of course only estimates, since the initial domain list is not complete, but it provides some impression for the size of the topic.
When did it start?
I have not yet done a systematic analysis, but it seems (based on
WHOIS
entries for some domain names) that this "capturing" of restaurant domain names has started already before the COVID-19 pandemic in 2019 and continued at least until 2022 and potentially still continues.
(Preliminary) Conclusions
The number of "lost" domain names provides evidence that German restaurants have been struggling in the 2019-2023 time frame. It would be interesting to revisit this analysis in one or two years to see who many more domain names have become inactive or taken over by lieferando.
Lieferando is using aggressive tactics to drive traffic to their site. Maybe this can be described as
growth hacking
or a way of
SEO
. It is apparently not even new.
The extend to which lieferando is using this method suggest that it is at least somewhat effective and probably quite cheap to implement.
💡
What are your thoughts on this topic? When you sign-in, you can let me know in the comments.

data.title: Bagel: Open-source unified multimodal model
data.author: tosh
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：开源多模态模型的性能、应用及其相关技术细节

不同观点：
• jjrv 分享了其在Ubuntu系统和RTX 3090 GPU上运行压缩版本模型的经验，指出该模型在硬件资源紧张的情况下勉强可以运行，但需要关闭其他窗口并降低屏幕分辨率。同时提到压缩版本与其原始版本结果应一致。
• spuz 对多模态模型中的“多模态”概念提出质疑，认为其通常只涉及文本和图像，而忽略了语音功能，并寻求能够结合语音功能的模型建议。
• akacrobat 对高质量开源多模态模型的稀缺表示认同，并询问社区是否有人对该模型进行过特定领域的微调实验。
• mdrzn 对模型的实际表现持怀疑态度，认为其在初步测试中未达到宣传效果，但仍希望其能实现所承诺的功能。
• charcircuit 对模型的性能提出批评，指出其在处理模糊问题时表现不佳，尤其在上下文理解和避免“幻觉”方面存在问题。

补充讨论：
• akoculu 提供了一个关于该模型的论文总结链接，供进一步了解。
• LourensT 对当前论文附带广告视频的现象进行了评论，暗示学术发布可能趋于商业化。
• GrantMoyer 强调该模型是Apache 2.0许可下的开源项目，指出了其开源性质。
• pleone 猜测该模型是否来自ByteDance团队，并询问社区对该团队的看法。
• mnky9800n 询问运行该模型所需的硬件配置，表明对硬件要求的关注。
• moffkalast 以幽默方式提到“The Everything Bagel”，可能意指模型功能的广泛性或复杂性。
• sandra_vu 询问该模型是否有商业化计划，表现出对模型未来发展的兴趣。
• wsintra2022 提供了一个相关新闻链接，可能包含更多讨论或背景信息。

争议焦点：
• 模型的实际性能与其宣传效果之间的差距是讨论中的一个争议点，mdrzn 和 charcircuit 均对此表示不满。
• 多模态模型是否应包括语音功能是另一个争议点，spuz 对此提出明确需求，但目前尚未有明确解决方案。

这些观点共同构成了对该多模态模型性能、应用及其技术细节的多角度讨论。

data.title: The truth about soft plastic recycling points at supermarkets
data.author: Kaibeezy
data.article_summary: 这篇文章揭示了英国超市软塑料回收计划的真相。调查追踪了40捆软塑料废物，发现其中70%被焚烧，而非回收，剩余部分则被降级回收为低价值产品，多数流向土耳其。环保组织ClientEarth警告，超市误导消费者。文章呼吁Sainsbury's和Tesco支持到2040年全球塑料生产减少40%，并推动减少一次性塑料包装，转向可重复使用系统。当前，全球正谈判制定《全球塑料条约》以应对塑料危害，文章鼓励公众签署请愿书以促进变革。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：软塑料回收及其替代处理方法（如焚烧）的有效性和可行性

不同观点：
• chimprich认为30%的软塑料被回收利用是一个不错的成果，并相信随着时间推移可以提高这一比例。他还认为，对已经分类好的塑料进行焚烧以回收能源是有效率的。
• stevep98指出一些特定产品，如Trex复合甲板，能够很好地利用回收的塑料，同时他也认为如果焚烧技术正确，焚烧并不是一个问题。
• PlunderBunny认为软塑料回收的结果取决于国家，如新西兰将软塑料回收制成围栏柱，并认为应进行研究而不是简单地否定或肯定回收。
• Scramblejams担心回收塑料中的有毒阻燃剂，认为在确保安全之前，埋葬塑料可能更安全。
• lotophage支持将塑料焚烧用于发电，因为塑料具有高能量含量，比褐煤更高效。
• meindnoch同样支持焚烧塑料，认为这样可以减少填埋，并减少对褐煤的开采。
• comrade1234指出在苏黎世只有PET塑料被回收，其他塑料都被焚烧发电，且二氧化碳被捕获再利用。
• Molitor5901认为应减少一次性塑料的使用，因为塑料难以回收，并提到自中国停止进口后，美国的塑料回收项目大多关闭。
• seanalltogether引用Penn和Teller的视频，认为只有玻璃和金属罐是真正的可回收产品。
• ninalanyon主张通过禁止塑料出口和非可再生塑料包装来加速塑料的减少和回收，并认为技术解决方案应由行业自行解决。
• Caelus9认为普通个人应尽量减少使用一次性塑料，但承认这在日常生活中具有挑战性。
• biofox认为将塑料转化为燃料颗粒也是一种回收形式，赋予其第二次生命。
• pfdietz建议将塑料分解回有用原料或单体，作为回收和焚烧之间的中间步骤，并认为应重点消除PVC等含氯塑料。

补充讨论：
• REDcycle在澳大利亚的失败案例（lotophage）显示出软塑料回收在实际操作中面临的困难。
• 关于焚烧技术的讨论，强调了现代焚烧设施的过滤和高效性（stevep98, comrade1234, worldsayshi）。
• 有关回收塑料的安全性问题，特别是与食品接触时的潜在风险（Scramblejams）。
• 强调政策和法规在推动塑料回收和减少使用中的作用（ninalanyon）。
• 不同地区对塑料回收和焚烧的处理方式不同，例如新西兰和苏黎世的案例（PlunderBunny, comrade1234）。

44095360.article_content:
Ever wondered what happens to the soft plastic that you return to the supermarket for recycling…?
…watch our film to find out
Share this video
Our new investigation reveals the
hard
truth about
soft
plastic recycling points at supermarkets…
🕵️ 40 bundles of soft plastic packaging waste were tracked through take-back schemes
across England over 12 months.
🔥 Of the tracked soft plastic packaging waste collected for recycling at Sainsbury's and Tesco stores,
70% of the soft plastic that reached a known destination was burnt, not recycled
🇹🇷 The rest ended up at recycling facilities that downcycle soft plastic waste into lower value products –
the majority of which were in Türkiye
.
⚠️ Environmental law NGO ClientEarth warns that the results of the investigation show that
supermarket soft plastic take-back schemes are misleading customers
.
🗣️ We’re now calling for Sainsbury's and Tesco to publicly support a
40% cut in global plastic production by 2040.
What happened to the soft plastic waste?
Collectively, these tracked bundles of soft plastic were found to have travelled over 25,000 km across the UK and overseas. Out of the trackers that we know reached a final destination…
What’s next?
The investigation shows that we urgently need to move away from false solutions.
We need to focus on eliminating unnecessary, non-essential single-use soft packaging and accelerating the transition to universally designed reuse and refill systems.
You can read our recommendations in full
.
Right now, world leaders are negotiating The Global Plastics Treaty – an international legal agreement to prevent the harmful impacts of plastic.
So we’re calling for the UK government to support a cut in global plastic production by 40% by 2040…
…and we want Sainsbury’s and Tesco to publicly support this.
✏️
You can help push for change. Add your voice now and sign our petition.
✏️
Already signed the petition? Click on the icons to share with your family, friends, colleagues, and community.
A bit of background
In 2021, supermarkets began to roll out an initiative to tackle the growing plastic problem – soft plastic packaging take-back schemes that claimed to help tackle the impact of plastic waste.
Supermarket communications around the schemes, along with revised on-pack recycling labelling, reassure customers that soft plastic is both recyclable and recycled – encouraging all of us to save up our salad bags, crisp packets, pasta packs, and pet food pouches at home, and drop it all off at supermarket collection points
.
Just over 10% of local councils collect soft plastic at the kerbside, and the waste industry widely acknowledges that there are significant challenges to recycling soft plastic.
"The truth is that finding a genuine solution for recycling soft plastic at scale is extremely difficult, if not impossible."
Sainsbury's and Tesco – between them – hold 43% market share of the UK supermarket sector. Both have widely rolled out soft plastic collection points to all their large stores. These take-back schemes encourage customers to collect their single-use soft plastic packaging at home and return it to the store, and are said to aim to increase recycling rates and reduce plastic waste.
Why is this important?
Plastic production is set to
triple by 2060
.
By 2050, global emissions from plastic production are estimated to account for
one-fifth of the Earth’s remaining carbon budget
.
Researchers warn that chemical pollution, also deriving from plastic use, threatens the stability of
global ecosystems and human health
.
Current estimates show that over
215 billion items
of soft plastic packaging are placed on the market each year in the UK
In 2022, only
7% of soft plastics
placed on the UK market were collected for recycling at the kerbside.

44095360.article_summary: 这篇文章揭示了英国超市软塑料回收计划的真相。调查追踪了40捆软塑料废物，发现其中70%被焚烧，而非回收，剩余部分则被降级回收为低价值产品，多数流向土耳其。环保组织ClientEarth警告，超市误导消费者。文章呼吁Sainsbury's和Tesco支持到2040年全球塑料生产减少40%，并推动减少一次性塑料包装，转向可重复使用系统。当前，全球正谈判制定《全球塑料条约》以应对塑料危害，文章鼓励公众签署请愿书以促进变革。
44095360.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：软塑料回收及其替代处理方法（如焚烧）的有效性和可行性

不同观点：
• chimprich认为30%的软塑料被回收利用是一个不错的成果，并相信随着时间推移可以提高这一比例。他还认为，对已经分类好的塑料进行焚烧以回收能源是有效率的。
• stevep98指出一些特定产品，如Trex复合甲板，能够很好地利用回收的塑料，同时他也认为如果焚烧技术正确，焚烧并不是一个问题。
• PlunderBunny认为软塑料回收的结果取决于国家，如新西兰将软塑料回收制成围栏柱，并认为应进行研究而不是简单地否定或肯定回收。
• Scramblejams担心回收塑料中的有毒阻燃剂，认为在确保安全之前，埋葬塑料可能更安全。
• lotophage支持将塑料焚烧用于发电，因为塑料具有高能量含量，比褐煤更高效。
• meindnoch同样支持焚烧塑料，认为这样可以减少填埋，并减少对褐煤的开采。
• comrade1234指出在苏黎世只有PET塑料被回收，其他塑料都被焚烧发电，且二氧化碳被捕获再利用。
• Molitor5901认为应减少一次性塑料的使用，因为塑料难以回收，并提到自中国停止进口后，美国的塑料回收项目大多关闭。
• seanalltogether引用Penn和Teller的视频，认为只有玻璃和金属罐是真正的可回收产品。
• ninalanyon主张通过禁止塑料出口和非可再生塑料包装来加速塑料的减少和回收，并认为技术解决方案应由行业自行解决。
• Caelus9认为普通个人应尽量减少使用一次性塑料，但承认这在日常生活中具有挑战性。
• biofox认为将塑料转化为燃料颗粒也是一种回收形式，赋予其第二次生命。
• pfdietz建议将塑料分解回有用原料或单体，作为回收和焚烧之间的中间步骤，并认为应重点消除PVC等含氯塑料。

补充讨论：
• REDcycle在澳大利亚的失败案例（lotophage）显示出软塑料回收在实际操作中面临的困难。
• 关于焚烧技术的讨论，强调了现代焚烧设施的过滤和高效性（stevep98, comrade1234, worldsayshi）。
• 有关回收塑料的安全性问题，特别是与食品接触时的潜在风险（Scramblejams）。
• 强调政策和法规在推动塑料回收和减少使用中的作用（ninalanyon）。
• 不同地区对塑料回收和焚烧的处理方式不同，例如新西兰和苏黎世的案例（PlunderBunny, comrade1234）。

data.title: How Does Claude 4 Think? – Sholto Douglas and Trenton Bricken
data.author: consumer451
data.article_summary: 这篇文章是Dwarkesh Podcast的一集，由主持人Dwarkesh Patel与Anthropic公司的Sholto Douglas和Trenton Bricken讨论Claude 4的思维机制。他们探讨了近年来AI研究的进展，包括强化学习（RL）的扩展、模型思维过程的追踪以及实现全自主智能体的路径。Sholto专注于RL的扩展，而Trenton则研究机械可解释性。他们提到RL在语言模型中的成功应用，尤其是在竞争性编程和数学领域，但尚未展示长期的智能体表现。此外，他们还讨论了各国、工作者和学生应如何为AGI（通用人工智能）的到来做好准备。文章最后提供了与赞助商相关的信息和时间戳。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：大型语言模型（LLMs）的现状、能力、局限以及未来发展

不同观点：
• **fumeux_fume** 认为LLMs的主要问题在于缺乏专家反馈，这反映了模型只是基于模式匹配进行猜测，而非真正理解。他还批评将LLMs与获得普利策奖或诺贝尔奖联系起来的炒作行为，并质疑有关AI发现新药的传闻，认为这是 hype 没有实质证据。
• **vessenes** 则关注于LLMs在实际应用中的潜力，特别是其在取代白领工作方面的能力，并认为当前技术已经足够成熟，可以在许多领域取代人类工作，这是一个重要的转折点。
• **crypto420** 引用了关于强化学习（RL）在LLMs中的扩展可能带来不可预测结果的观点，并认为未来10-20年可能会出现非常不可预测的技术突破，甚至可能走向奇点（Singularity）。

补充讨论：
• **dcre** 强调通过这类访谈可以高效了解前沿技术的发展，并提供了之前类似访谈的链接以供参考。
• **arecurrence** 表示对访谈中讨论的当前技术挑战很感兴趣，并赞赏访谈中提供的论文链接，认为这有助于深入理解相关主题。
• **Der_Einzige** 关注于具体技术细节，质疑为何2019年发明的更好的采样方法（tail free sampling）至今未被广泛应用，并呼吁发明者给出解释。
• **cratermoon** 简短指出LLMs并不具备思考能力，这是一个直截了当的技术能力界定。
• **binary132** 只是简单提及了访谈的制作方，没有深入讨论内容。

争议焦点：
• LLMs是否只是基于模式匹配进行猜测，还是具备某种程度的理解能力（fumeux_fume vs. 其他观点）。
• 有关AI发现新药的传闻是否可信，是否是炒作。
• 强化学习在LLMs中的应用是否会导致不可预测且潜在危险的结果。

这些讨论反映了不同参与者对LLMs现状及其未来发展的多样化观点和关注点。

Dwarkesh Patel
Okay. I'm joined again by my friends, Sholto Bricken... Wait, fuck. Did I do this

.

, Trenton's still working on
mechanistic interpretability

What's changed since last year?
We talked basically this month in 2024
.
Sholto Douglas
Yep.
Dwarkesh Patel
Now, we're in 2025. What's happened?
Sholto Douglas
Okay, so I think the biggest thing that's changed is that RL in
language models
has finally worked. We finally have proof of an algorithm that can give us expert human reliability and performance, given the right feedback loop. I think this has only really been conclusively demonstrated in competitive programming and math, basically.
Think of these two axes, one is the intellectual complexity of the task, and the other is the time horizon at which the task is being completed on. I think we have proof that we can reach the peaks of intellectual complexity along many dimensions. We haven't yet demonstrated long-running
agentic performance
. You're seeing the first stumbling steps of that now, and should see much more conclusive evidence of that basically by the end of the year, with real software engineering agents doing real work. I think Trenton, you're experimenting with this at the moment?

Yeah, absolutely. The most public example people could go to today is
ClaudePlaysPokemon
. Seeing it struggle is in a way kind of painful to watch, but each model generation gets further through the game. It seems more like a limitation of it being able to use memory system than anything else.
Dwarkesh Patel
I wish we had recorded predictions last year. We definitely should this year.
Trenton Bricken
Hold us accountable.

data.title: Show HN: A minimalist web timer for focus and time tracking
data.author: StephenAlvin
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对一个时间管理工具的评价与建议，涉及工具的功能、设计、实用性以及是否符合“极简主义”的定义。

不同观点：
• [ProllyInfamous] 提到该工具导致浏览器崩溃，提出了技术问题，并提供了联系方式以获取更多信息。
• [bryanhogan] 分享了自己开发的类似工具，强调了其工具的本地化、非盈利性质和极简设计，用于时间盒管理。
• [susam] 称赞了该项目，并介绍了自己的IRC based timer 't0'，强调了社区互动和学习资源的发现。
• [clamlady] 作为非营利组织工作者，认为该工具对项目时间追踪很有帮助，并对工具的极简性质表示赞赏。
• [newlisp] 提到广告拦截器迅速增加，感觉像在访问YouTube，暗示广告较多。
• [rpastuszak] 对工具的暗色背景表示喜欢，并提出了对功能改进的建议，如模糊自动完成和快捷键，同时分享了自己开发的类似工具。
• [fleebee] 和 [furkansahin]、[KingEllis]、[heavyshark] 对工具是否符合“极简主义”提出质疑，认为工具页面上的分享功能和边框设计不够极简。
• [noufalibrahim] 分享了自己开发的类似工具，强调了任务时间估算和日志记录功能。
• [rckt] 质疑为何需要一个网页应用来追踪时间，认为如果没有网络功能，网页应用没有必要，除非是为了练习编码技能。
• [vanschelven] 提到工具背景动画导致CPU占用过高，浏览器插件关闭了标签页。
• [Klaster_1] 分享了自己的计时器项目，强调本地化、PWA性质和基本统计功能，项目已使用超过10年。
• [tra3] 提出需要一种能够 retrospectively 记录活动的应用，因为经常忘记启动计时器。

补充讨论：
- 争议焦点在于该工具是否真正符合“极简主义”的定义，部分用户认为分享功能和设计元素与极简主义相悖。
- 用户对工具的功能改进提出了建议，如模糊自动完成、快捷键、以及对忘记启动计时器的解决方案。
- 一些用户分享了自己开发的类似工具，强调了本地化、非盈利性质和特定的功能改进。
- 技术问题如浏览器崩溃和CPU占用过高也被提及，影响了用户体验。

data.title: Big banks explore venturing into crypto world together with joint stablecoin
data.author: wslh
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：stablecoins的用途、优势、争议及其与传统银行系统的关系

不同观点：
• **支持stablecoins的观点**：
  - **可编程货币**：[scyclow] 指出stablecoins允许可编程货币，避免了传统加密货币价格波动的问题。例如，可以通过智能合约实现特定条件下的资金转移。
  - **效率提升**：部分评论认为stablecoins比传统银行系统更快、更有效，特别是在跨境交易和规避旧技术限制方面具有优势。

• **质疑stablecoins的观点**：
  - **银行参与的必要性**：[highfrequency] 质疑如果银行能够解决技术和监管问题，是否还有必要使用stablecoins作为USD的包装。
  - **合法性和监管问题**：[thunkle] 提出World Liberty Financial与特朗普家族及中东特使的资金关联，质疑其中潜在的利益冲突和合法性问题。
  - **潜在风险**：[Ekaros] 认为stablecoins可能被用于拒绝归还用户资金，这在传统货币系统中更难实现。

• **对stablecoins未来发展的看法**：
  - **竞争与整合**：[Mengkudulangsat] 认为stablecoins市场正在经历一场“逐底竞争”，从Tether到Circle再到传统银行，未来可能由美联储发行最权威的stablecoins。
  - **不可避免的银行参与**：[nailer] 认为银行最终会想要创建和持有自己的stablecoin，以在市场中占据一席之地。

• **对银行系统的信任**：
  - **对银行系统的批评**：[jbs789] 指出银行的缓慢部分是因为反洗钱(AML)和了解客户(KYC)的控制措施，而这些控制措施同样适用于stablecoins。
  - **银行创造货币的能力**：[_heimdall] 认为美国银行已经能够快速创造货币，因此stablecoins的必要性不明确。

补充讨论：
• **对整体金融环境的担忧**：[nickysielicki] 对财政部可能导致stablecoins系统崩溃表示担忧，质疑stablecoins相对于传统货币的稳定性。
• **与Ripple/XRP的比较**：[thatguyagain] 提到Ripple/XRP的初衷是为银行提供快速和安全的交易，质疑银行为什么不自己创建网络而是依赖第三方。
• **对评论质量的批评**：[monero-xmr] 批评Hacker News/YC在加密货币领域的讨论质量，认为很多并购活动未被正确理解。

争议的焦点：
• stablecoins是否真正提供了比传统银行系统更有效、更安全的解决方案，还是仅仅是现有系统的重复。
• stablecoins的合法性和潜在风险，特别是在利益冲突和资金安全方面的问题。
