More
8
1
Share
“Dover” (1975) by Deborah Remington, giving HAL 9000 vibes in the Phoenix Art Museum
Last summer I
made the case
for bringing the principle of
Dune
’s Butlerian Jihad — “Thou shalt not make a machine in the likeness of a human mind” — to our broader discourse on AI. It seemed like a good way to bind together the various felt and thought objections to AI into a common credo. And a good way to distinguish between benign forms of so-called “AI” (spotting tumors, for instance) and the
sycophantic
imitations of humanity being peddled by the various broligarchs.
Since then, this “hard no” movement against AI has started to take shape. For one the
t-shirt game
keeps getting better.
Traps are being set
on the internet to punish AI scrapers and poison datasets. The
new Chicago pope bashed AI
in his first big speech. Just in my literary corner of the world, anti-AI clauses are becoming standard in book contracts and magazine submission forms. A recent episode of AppleTV’s
The Studio
ended with a crowd at ComicCon — and Ice Cube — chanting “fuck AI.” Last week there was a
WorldCon kerfuffle
(sigh) over using ChatGPT in part of the panel selection process.
(My WorldCon take is that, well intentioned though it was, feeding an AI a list of names and asking it to compile dossiers of their scandals and transgressions is a pretty dystopian use-case.)
It’s clear that writers, artists, and others in that orbit increasingly view any amount of engagement with LLMs as a betrayal of creative class solidarity. The sentiment (which I’ve heard all the way from Tumblr teens to Pulitzer Prize winners) seems to be something like this:
A famous panel from Frank Miller’s
The Dark Knight Returns
.
I’ve heard pushback about such anti-AI puritanism, the ways it’s just another case of social media mob culture. For me, this is where the Butlerian Jihad continues to be a fruitful metaphor. The
Dune
books are all about how holy wars and revolutions are not gentle or reasonable, how they can turn ugly, righteousness fueling a fire that can consume nations and worlds.
The other way the metaphor is proving apt is the deep-seated, almost spiritual nature of anti-AI sentiment. It’s not just more Luddism. Many people — though hardly all, given the popularity of AI products — sense that there is something grotesque about these simulacra, the people who push them on us, this whole affair. That aversion to the technological profane holds even when various stated objections to AI are supposedly addressed or nitpicked to death.
1
Meanwhile, throughout all this, I have myself felt on the front lines of something like a grand struggle against these likeness machines —  not just as a creative but as a teacher. Because what’s become clear over the past year is that the killer app, the median American use case for products like ChatGPT, is cheating on your homework.
There’s been a lot written about this lately — a big article
dropped in New York Mag
as I was sitting down to type this newsletter, and a discord mutual had a
similarly thorough piece a couple weeks ago in the Chronicle of Higher Education
. Both pieces get into the increasing AI frustration among teachers and the increasing AI dependency among students.
There was a lot of hope for the value of AI in education (and still is, if university partnerships with tech companies are any measure). An infinitely patient digital tutor that can tackle any question (a la the Primer in Neal Stephenson’s
Diamond Age
, and probably a hundred other SF references)
sounds
like just what a strained education system needs — if it didn’t hallucinate constantly, that is. And I know teachers who use it. They’ll have students check with ChatGPT in class to get answers to discussion questions, or encourage its use in revision. Some are no doubt having AI write emails to students and paper feedback, too.
But these articles show that concern is mounting over a few factors. First, there’s a big difference between getting something explained to you, and actual learning. You might
feel
like you are learning when querying a chatbot, but those intellectual gains are often illusory.
Second, AI severs the connection between an output, like an essay, and the real learning, thinking, and practice creating that output usually requires. There’s now no way to be sure that a student who turns in a good essay actually has a grasp on the material that assignment was supposed to push them toward understanding. Thus, AI lets students skip the “desirable difficulties” that produce real learning. The temptation to skip these difficulties is powerful enough that even very engaged

data.title: The Difference Between Downloading and Streaming
data.author: kruemmelspalter
data.article_summary: 本文简要解释了流媒体（streaming）和下载（downloading）视频、音频等线性媒体之间的区别。尽管许多平台强调两者不同，但从技术角度看，它们基本相同。无论是流媒体还是下载，服务器都会将视频帧发送到设备，设备在播放时会暂时存储这些帧。区别在于设备如何处理这些帧：如果播放后删除，称为流媒体；如果保存为文件，则称为下载。流媒体过程中，视频播放器会预先缓存部分帧，以防止网络波动影响观看体验，因此从某种意义上说，所有流媒体都是下载。平台声称不能下载媒体，实际上依赖于用户设备在观看后删除文件的“诚信原则”。然而，用户有多种方法可以保留流媒体副本。尽管流媒体和下载在某些技术细节上（如文件顺序和压缩方式）存在差异，但从服务器角度看，它们非常相似。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点： streaming与downloading的区别及其技术实现，包括协议选择、延迟处理、业务需求以及语言使用上的争议。

不同观点：
• [schoen] 认为流媒体历史上使用不可靠传输协议（如UDP）以避免重传，尤其在实时传输中，旧数据帧的丢失不影响观看体验。但现代流媒体通过缓冲和TCP协议实现了更可靠的传输，即便有一定延迟。实时双向通信（如电话、Zoom会议）仍依赖UDP以保持低延迟。
• [ryandrake] 强调流媒体与下载在技术上没有本质区别，早期客户期望视频流媒体不支持下载是误解。流媒体本质上就是边下载边播放。
• [Cyphase] 指出普通用户对“下载”和“流媒体”的认知存在误解，比如将浏览网页视为非下载行为，尽管技术上这确实是下载。
• [NoPicklez] 认为流媒体和下载的区别更多在于用户意图和技术实现方式，流媒体强调实时播放，下载则侧重获取完整内容并保存。
• [wood_spirit] 提出音乐流媒体和下载的区别更多是商业许可问题，而非技术差异。
• [nntwozz] 从个人经验出发，强调下载的重要性，并列举了多种下载工具。
• [Hashex129542] 详细区分了流媒体和下载的技术流程，包括本地和远程数据处理方式的不同。
• [lukax] 提到Koofr用户曾要求防止从公共链接下载文件，但实际上只能隐藏下载按钮，无法真正阻止下载行为。
• [Animats] 指出一些“流媒体”系统实际上是通过JavaScript将短视频片段拼接成长视频，以实现使用HTTPS协议的流媒体功能。
• [voilavilla] 认为版权保护策略并非注定失败，未来所有媒体设备将采用更安全的信任链和加密技术，以防止未经授权的复制。
• [haddr] 询问是否有浏览器能够在显示流媒体内容之前先存储并解码。
• [ljsprague] 认为上述讨论是显而易见的。
• [dusted] 强调讨论流媒体和下载时应忽略传输层，流媒体是下载的一个子集，低层次的流媒体是数据传输的过程，高层次的流媒体则是边加载边播放并丢弃已播放的数据。

补充讨论：
• HDCP 2.3是否已被破解的问题在评论中被提出，但未有明确答案。
• 流媒体和下载在技术上是否存在本质区别存在争议，部分评论者认为仅是术语和用户意图的不同，而非技术差异。
• 实时双向通信的低延迟需求与流媒体的缓冲机制之间的矛盾被提出，Zoom等应用仍依赖UDP以保持低延迟。

44101072.article_content:
What’s the difference between “streaming” and “downloading” video, audio, or some other kind of linear media?
1
Many platforms make a firm distinction between streaming and downloading, implying that they’re very different. But they’re not.
They’re basically the same thing
Despite what various platforms would have you believe, there’s no significant
technical
difference between streaming and downloading.
Suppose you’re choosing whether to download or stream a video
2
.
In both cases
3
:
The server gets frames of video from a source (file, livestream, etc.)
The server sends those frames to your device
Your device stores them while it does something with them
Want to keep a copy of this animation? You don’t have to trick your computer into retaining it as it streams because
I’ve open-sourced it, and the code used to produce it
.
So what’s the difference?
The fundamental difference between streaming and downloading is what
your device
does with those frames of video:
Does it show them to you once and then throw them away? Or does it re-assemble them all back into a video file and save it into storage?
When you’re streaming on YouTube, the video player running on your computer retains a buffer of frames ahead and behind of your current position, so you can skip around easily: the
darker grey part of the timeline shows which parts of the video are stored on – that is,
downloaded
to – your computer.
Buffering
is when your streaming player gets some number of frames “ahead” of where you’re watching, to give you some protection against connection issues. If your WiFi wobbles
for a moment, the buffer protects you from the video stopping completely for a few seconds.
But for buffering to work, your computer
has
to retain bits of the video. So in a very real sense,
all
streaming
is
downloading! The buffer is the part
of the stream that’s downloaded onto your computer right now. The question is: what happens to it next?
All streaming
is
downloading
So that’s the bottom line: if your computer
deletes
the frames of video it was storing in the buffer, we call that streaming. If it
retains
them in a file, we
call that downloading.
That definition introduces a philosophical problem. Remember that Vimeo checkbox that lets a creator decide whether people can (i.e. are allowed to) download their videos?
Isn’t
that somewhat meaningless if
all streaming is downloading
.
Because if the difference between streaming and downloading is whether their device belonging to the person
watching
the video deletes the media when they’re done. And in
virtually all cases, that’s done on the honour system.
This kind of conversation happens, over the HTTP protocol,
all the time
. Probably most of the time the browser is telling the truth, but there’s no way to know for certain.
When your favourite streaming platform says that it’s only possible to stream, and not download, their media… or when they restrict “downloading” as an option to higher-cost paid plans…
they’re relying on the assumption that the user’s device can be trusted to delete the media when the user’s done watching it.
But a user who owns their own device, their own network, their own screen or speakers has many, many opportunities to not fulfil the promise of deleting media it after they’ve consumed
it: to retain a “downloaded” copy for their own enjoyment, including:
Intercepting the media as it passes through their network on the way to its destination device
Using client software that’s been configured to stream-and-save, rather than steam-and-delete, the content
Modifying “secure” software (e.g. an official app) so that it retains a saved copy rather than deleting it
Capturing the stream buffer as it’s cached in device memory or on the device’s hard disk
Outputting the resulting media to a different device, e.g. using a HDMI capture device, and saving it there
Exploiting the “analogue
4
hole”
5
:
using a camera, microphone, etc. to make a copy of what comes out of the screen/speakers
6
Okay, so I oversimplified (before you say “well, actually…”)
It’s not entirely true to say that streaming and downloading are
identical
, even with the caveat of “…from the server’s perspective”. There are three big exceptions worth
thinking about:
Exception #1: downloads can come in any order
When you stream some linear media, you
expect
the server to send the media in strict chronological order. Being able to start watching
before the whole file has
downloaded
is a big part of what makes steaming appealing, to the end-user. This means that media
intended for streaming
tends to be stored in a way that facilitates that
kind of delivery. For example:
Media designed for streaming will often be stored in linear chronological order in the file, which impacts what kinds of compression are available.
Media designed for streaming will generally use formats that put file metadata at the
start
of the file, so that it gets delivered first.
Video designed for streaming will often have frequent keyframes

• [lukax] 提到Koofr用户曾要求防止从公共链接下载文件，但实际上只能隐藏下载按钮，无法真正阻止下载行为。
• [Animats] 指出一些“流媒体”系统实际上是通过JavaScript将短视频片段拼接成长视频，以实现使用HTTPS协议的流媒体功能。
• [voilavilla] 认为版权保护策略并非注定失败，未来所有媒体设备将采用更安全的信任链和加密技术，以防止未经授权的复制。
• [haddr] 询问是否有浏览器能够在显示流媒体内容之前先存储并解码。
• [ljsprague] 认为上述讨论是显而易见的。
• [dusted] 强调讨论流媒体和下载时应忽略传输层，流媒体是下载的一个子集，低层次的流媒体是数据传输的过程，高层次的流媒体则是边加载边播放并丢弃已播放的数据。

补充讨论：
• HDCP 2.3是否已被破解的问题在评论中被提出，但未有明确答案。
• 流媒体和下载在技术上是否存在本质区别存在争议，部分评论者认为仅是术语和用户意图的不同，而非技术差异。
• 实时双向通信的低延迟需求与流媒体的缓冲机制之间的矛盾被提出，Zoom等应用仍依赖UDP以保持低延迟。

data.title: Claude 4 and GitHub MCP will leak your private GitHub repositories
data.author: amrrs
data.article_summary: 文章提到，在x.com网站上，一些与隐私相关的浏览器扩展程序可能会引发问题。建议用户禁用这些扩展程序，然后重试访问网站。文章提醒用户不必担心，问题通常可以通过这个方法解决。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：GitHub Copilot和大型语言模型（LLM）在处理私人代码和敏感信息时的安全性问题

不同观点：
• **kapitanjakc** 分享了一个具体案例，指出GitHub Copilot可能在未经授权的情况下读取私人代码库，并复制到其他项目中。他认为这可能已经持续了一段时间，并通过自己遇到的相似代码案例说明了问题。

• **losvedir** 认为，问题在于用户给LLM的访问权限过大。他指出，GitHub有细粒度的访问控制，用户应生成仅限于特定仓库的访问令牌，以减少风险。如果LLM拥有全局访问权限，那么问题更可能出在用户的安全实践上，而不是工具本身。

• **theptip** 提出了一种新的解决方案，建议使用分区子代理来隔离不同类型的任务，比如公共和私人代码库的交互。这类似于网络安全中的防火墙和安全边界概念。

• **adeon** 从安全角度出发，认为如果LLM能够从不可信的来源获取文本输入，那么这些输入可能会被用来操纵LLM生成任意文本，从而调用工具。他提到Invariant Labs提供的防护产品，并质疑AI公司是否在设计时就考虑了安全性。

• **ttoinou** 建议用户能够对每个查询精细控制LLM的访问权限，比如开启或关闭记忆功能、查询历史、连接的应用等。他认为这样可以有效减少潜在的安全风险。

• **ed** 不认为这是LLM的攻击行为，而是建议GitHub考虑引入私人草案PR机制，以便在发布前有人工审核。

• **foerster** 分享了自己遇到的情况，指出Bingbot流量请求了私人函数，这可能是Copilot或OpenAI导致的问题。

• **BeetleB** 表示只使用自己编写的MCP工具，因为审计第三方代码太费时，即使是来自“可信”组织的代码。

• **rcleveng** 开玩笑地问是否GitHub的MCP服务器代码也是由AI编写的。

• **shwouchk** 通过实验展示了LLM在不受限制的情况下可以执行的各种操作，包括提交Git代码、添加GitHub Action等。他认为这可能导致新的安全漏洞。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于LLM和Copilot是否在未经授权的情况下访问和使用私人代码。部分用户认为这是用户安全实践不当所致，而其他人则认为工具本身应具备更多的防护措施。
• 讨论中多次提到需要更好的访问控制和防护机制，比如细粒度的权限管理和防护产品。
• 有用户对LLM的潜在滥用表示担忧，认为随着技术的发展，安全问题可能会变得更加严重。

data.title: Changelog: Lazy trees (faster Nix builds)
data.author: internet_points
data.article_summary: 2025年5月15日，Luc Perkins 发布了一篇关于 **Changelog** 的文章，介绍了 **Lazy Trees** 这一新功能。Lazy Trees 是 **Determinate Nix** 项目的一部分，旨在优化 Nix 构建过程。通过延迟加载和按需计算，Lazy Trees 能够显著减少内存占用并提高构建速度。这一改进对于处理大型项目和复杂依赖关系尤为重要，有助于增强 Nix 的可扩展性和性能表现。Lazy Trees 还简化了并行构建的实现，为开发者提供了更高效的构建体验。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Nix 生态中的 Flakes 和 Lazy Trees 功能，及其对 monorepos 的影响和社区接受度

不同观点：
• [dmvinson 的观点]
  ◦ Flakes 的 lazy trees 是一个期待已久的改变，特别是在 monorepos 中，没有它 Flakes 几乎不可用。
  ◦ 尽管 Flakes 不是理想的解决方案，但 Nix 社区常常因为追求完美而忽视了改进的机会。
  ◦ Nix 社区需要提出一个标准化的方式来固定渠道（pinning channels），否则社区没有其他可行的替代标准。
  ◦ 目前像 niv 这样的工具虽然能解决问题，但过于小众，不能满足大多数用户的需求。

• [cosmic_quanta 的观点]
  ◦ 对 Nix 语言语义的改变可能是实现 lazy trees 性能提升的前提条件。
  ◦ 对 Nix 语言不够熟悉，因此对性能提升的具体实现和效果持保留态度。
  ◦ 尽管有疑问，但对技术进展表示认可和兴趣。

补充讨论：
• [dmvinson] 认为 Nix 社区如果不喜欢 Flakes 或 DetSys，应该提出替代方案，否则继续使用 Flakes 是合理的选择。
• [cosmic_quanta] 关注 lazy trees 的性能提升在实际应用中可能不会如宣传的那样显著，因为这涉及到对 Nix 语言的语义更改。
• 争议的焦点在于 lazy trees 的实际效果和 Nix 社区对 Flakes 的接受度，以及是否需要一个更广泛认可的标准来替代 Flakes。

总体来看，讨论围绕着 Nix 生态中的技术改进和社区对这些改进的接受程度展开。

data.title: Duolingo CEO tries to walk back AI-first comments, fails
data.author: Improvement
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Duolingo的学习效果、商业模式、AI应用及其对产品质量的影响

不同观点：
• [lolinder] 认为Duolingo越来越注重通过操纵用户的注意力（如连续登录奖励等游戏化手段）来提高用户粘性，而不是帮助用户有效学习。其妻子在使用多年后因感觉学习效果下降而退出，并认为Duolingo早已偏离了其最初的教育使命。
• [eigenspace] 批评Duolingo的内容过于大众化，缺乏深度，推荐使用像Seedlang这样更注重真实语言环境的小众学习平台。Seedlang通过真实视频和语音回放帮助用户更有效地练习发音和听力。
• [amsilprotag] 指出Duolingo的用户体验问题，例如过多的弹出广告和无意义的成就展示，认为Busuu等其他平台在内容质量和用户体验上更胜一筹。
• [whyowhy3484939] 对技术在语言学习中的作用持怀疑态度，认为过度依赖技术反而导致学习效果下降，并引用多篇文章支持其观点，呼吁人们不要过度依赖技术解决非技术问题。
• [godzillabrennus] 对Duolingo用AI替代人类课程作者的做法感到失望，认为AI技术不应取代人类在教育中的核心作用，并表示将寻找其他低成本的AI工具进行语言学习。
• [in_ab] 担心AI的广泛应用会导致软件质量的下降，认为许多公司试图用AI替代人类劳动力可能会引发负面后果。
• [i80and] 表示尽管曾付费使用Duolingo，但在得知人类课程作者被AI取代后立即停止了订阅，强调付费服务应由人类提供而非AI。
• [BrandiATMuhkuh] 从学术研究和个人经验出发，认为语言学习的关键在于社会互动，AI难以替代人与人之间的互动和交流，并提出理想的语言学习应用应模仿儿童语言习得的方式。
• [hiAndrewQuinn] 介绍了自己开发的针对芬兰语学习者的开源软件，并表示通过这些工具不仅帮助了自己，还建立了专业联系，展示了小众语言学习工具的价值。
• [thenberlin] 认为如果AI可以完全替代人类教师，那么Duolingo这样的中间商平台就没有存在的必要，批评公司过度依赖AI可能会导致整个商业模式的崩溃。
• [landl0rd] 持悲观态度，认为消费者行为难以改变，尽管有用户不满Duolingo的质量下降，但大多数人仍会继续使用，公司也会继续推行其策略。
• [bayareapsycho] 从金融角度分析Duolingo的高市盈率，认为公司目前的主要目标是维持股价和吸引投资，而非提高产品质量。
• [InTheArena] 认为AI将颠覆整个软件行业，Duolingo的AI转型是行业趋势的一部分，不可避免。
• [foxfired] 通过个人经历揭示了企业追逐技术潮流的现象，指出许多技术宣传只是为了短期商业利益，而非真正改进产品。

补充讨论：
- Duolingo的游戏化设计（如连续登录奖励）被批评为过度注重用户粘性而忽视学习效果。
- 多个评论提到AI替代人类劳动力可能导致产品质量下降，并对AI在教育中的应用持怀疑态度。
- 不同用户推荐了其他语言学习平台，如Seedlang和Busuu，认为这些平台在内容和用户体验上优于Duolingo。
- 有评论从金融和商业模式角度分析Duolingo的策略，认为其主要目标是吸引投资和维持股价，而非提高教育质量。
- 争议焦点在于AI在语言学习中的应用是否能替代人类教师，以及Duolingo是否应继续依赖游戏化手段吸引用户。

data.author: signa11
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了Rust和Zig语言中的类型系统，特别是Zig中"类型即值"的特性。Zig允许在编译时对类型进行操作，例如通过函数生成条件类型如`ListIfOddLength`。然而，这种灵活性可能导致类型签名中包含过多逻辑，使得代码难以理解和推理。相比之下，Hindley-Milner类型系统通过限制类型的复杂性，提供了更人性化的体验，并支持强大的类型推断。虽然Zig的编译时运行功能有其优势，但作者认为可以结合Zig的优点与Hindley-Milner的舒适性，实现更友好的编程语言设计。作者还提出了编译时已知变量的原则，强调编译器应跟踪这些变量而不将其混入类型系统。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：类型的本质及其在编程语言中的表示与使用

不同观点：
• **codebje** 认为类型的本质是一个哲学问题，区分了类型是否应作为值来处理。他主张类型是规格说明（specification），而非实现（implementation），并以类型擦除（type erasure）为例说明某些语言中类型在运行时并不作为值存在。他还提出，值是程序运行时所操作的数据，而类型则属于不同的语义范畴。他认为类型到值的映射（如Hindley-Milner类型系统中的参数多态）是可行的，但从值到类型的映射则较为复杂且少见。

• **burakemir** 提到了Racket语言的多阶段编程（multistage programming）以及其在类型系统和逻辑中的表示。他指出，多阶段编程通过在运行时表示代码来实现，且已经有相关研究和实践，如Scala中的宏和多阶段编程，这些都涉及到如何在类型系统中表示程序。

• **aatd86** 对讨论的核心内容感到困惑，并尝试简化问题。他提出了几种可能性，包括高阶类型（higher kinded types）、类型检查的可判定性问题、类型是否作为一等值存在于语言的前端，以及类型是否被定义为值的集合。

补充讨论：
• **关于类型与值的哲学讨论**：codebje深入探讨了类型与值的关系，包括类型是否可以作为值、类型的类型是什么，以及这种区分是否有意义。他提到了类型系统的一致性与完备性问题，并认为依赖类型系统（dependent type system）可能是实现足够表达力且一致的类型系统的途径。

• **关于编译时与运行时的代码执行**：codebje进一步讨论了在编译时评估常量表达式的概念，并以C++中的constexpr为例，说明编译时计算的可能性。他还提到了部分求值（partial evaluation）的概念，这是一种将程序的静态部分在编译时求值的技术，可以用来优化程序执行。

• **关于多阶段编程与宏**：burakemir补充了多阶段编程的实际应用例子，如Racket的宏和Scala的相关实现。这些例子展示了如何在类型系统中表示和操作运行时的代码。

争议焦点：
• 主要争议在于类型是否应作为值处理，以及这种处理在实际编程语言中的可行性和意义。codebje和burakemir提供了不同的视角和实际例子，而aatd86则对讨论的核心内容提出了简化和澄清的请求。

44086935.article_content:
D
erin Eryılmaz
Having your compile-time cake and eating it too
May 24, 2025
Disclaimer
In this post, I assume:
You know a little bit about Rust.
You know a little bit about Zig.
I'll be using my own syntax to express ideas from both of these languages.
Why "types are just values" doesn't work
As programmers, we like it when our programs run well.
Type systems are there to help us with that. They track the types of values in our programs before we run them, which not only saves us from runtime crashes but enforces guidelines for writing good code.
Normally, type syntax (and logic) is distinct from the rest of a programming language. A rare exception to this rule is Zig, where types are just treated as values, and compile-time (comptime) operations on those values are allowed. That's all the type system is.
In a normal language, the
List[Int]
type is a very abstract idea. But in Zig,
List(Int)
is just a regular function call where you're inputting a
Type
and getting a
Type
back. Simple, right?
Well, if we can make a
List
function, why not a
ListIfOddLength
function that's a bit more powerful?
ListIfOddLength = (T: Type) => Type: (
if (T.to_string.length % 2 == 1) then List(T) else T
)
Okay, now let's make a generic function using it. (Square brackets introduce a type parameter.)
weird_function = [T](value: T) => ListIfOddLength(T): (
...
)
The function above takes a value with some type (
T
). If that type has an odd length, it'll return a
List(T)
, and otherwise it'll just return a
T
.
While it may not be useful,
Zig lets us express this sort of idea
. The problem is that now you're putting arbitrary logic into a type signature. To understand what type
weird_function
returns, you'll need to understand exactly how
ListIfOddLength
works. You'd have to know what
%
means and what
to_string
does.
Let's do more silly examples. Imagine that
ListIfBHash(T)
turns
T
into a string, then hashes it. The function usually returns
T
, but it'll return
List(T)
if the hash starts with a B. Or what about
ListIfAmerica
, which returns a
List(T)
if you're compiling from the United States?
With silly type-to-type functions like this, you lose the ability to reason about your program. This could be a line in your code:
y = weird_function(x)
And it could take some time to figure out the type of
y
, even if you knew what the type of
x
was. This is bad, because
type systems have to work for humans.
We see values and variables as logical things. We want to be able to express what they are in a simple way, so that we can explain them to others and understand them ourselves. Letting any operation be done on any type makes this impossible and makes a type system human-unfriendly by allowing stuff like
weird_function
.
Luckily for us, human-friendly type systems have already been invented. The most popular one is called
Hindley-Milner
(HM), and it's used by many big languages, including Swift, Rust, Scala, Haskell, OCaml, and more. (You don't need to be able to read type theory to know what HM means; just imagine the types you could write in your favorite language from that list.)
Hindley-Milner doesn't treat types as values; it treats them as abstract things that are limited to being (possibly generic) structs or enums.
By giving up that flexibility:
No more
weird_function
or
ListIfBHash
allowed.
All legal type signatures can be expressed without arbitrary logic.
Very strong type inference is supported, to the point where you almost never have to specify types.
However, Zig's comptime and type system allow for some capabilities that most HM languages can't replicate. And the ones that can (like Rust) use macros to do it, which introduces a second syntax and a whole lot of confusion.
I've seen people say Zig's features don't mix with a human-friendly type system, but I just don't think that's true. My goal in this post is to show that it's possible for a language to adopt many of them while keeping the comfort of Hindley-Milner.
Running code at compile-time
Principles:
Certain variables are known at compile-time, and the compiler should keep track of which ones are.
Most functions can be run at compile-time.
A few functions can
only
be run at compile-time.
Programmers should have to explicitly run things at compile-time. The language shouldn't do it for them.
(Keep in mind that when I call things "variables" in this blog post, I don't mean they can change. This stuff works best for a language with mostly immutable variables.)
In my opinion, the compiler should keep track of comptime-known variables, but not as part of the type system. The basic rules are simple: number/string literals are comptime-known, but function results are not.
// known
eight = 8
// not known
eight_fac = factorial(8)
An expression can be forced with
@
to make its result known at compile-time.
// known
eight_fac = @(factorial(8))
// shorter syntax
eight_fac = @factorial(8)
// another short syntax
eight_fac @= factorial(8)
These would be the same as typing
eight_fac

data.title: Mutmut – Python Mutation Tester
data.author: e-topy
data.article_summary: Mutmut是一个用于Python的变异测试系统，注重易用性。它能够将发现的变异直接应用到磁盘，支持增量工作，并能识别需要执行的测试以加快变异测试速度。它具有交互式终端界面，支持并行快速执行。Mutmut要求在有fork支持的系统上运行，Windows用户需使用WSL。安装和运行简单，通过`pip install mutmut`和`mutmut run`命令即可开始。用户可以在变异结果中查看、重新测试变异，并将变异应用到代码中。配置文件`setup.cfg`或`pyproject.toml`中可设置变异路径、测试目录等选项。系统支持Unix文件名模式匹配、限制堆栈深度以加快测试速度，并允许排除特定文件或代码行的变异。变异示例包括改变整数文字和比较运算符等。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：变异测试（mutation testing）的适用性和价值

不同观点：
• MichaelNolan认为变异测试是一个很好的想法，但对具体库不熟悉，仅在Java项目中使用过PiTest。他指出，变异测试在共享库代码中非常有用，能增强对代码正确性的信心。
• 然而，MichaelNolan也提到，决定哪些代码值得进行变异测试是一个难点。他认为许多“业务”代码可能不适合这种测试方式，因为编写测试所付出的努力可能超过所得回报。

补充讨论：
• MichaelNolan具体说明了变异测试在不同类型代码中的适用性差异。他强调，对于共享库代码，变异测试能够提供更高的价值和信心，而对于一般的业务代码，可能并不划算。
• 他还隐含指出了一个争议焦点，即投入与产出的平衡问题。对于某些类型的代码，进行变异测试可能并不实际或经济。

总结来看，评论主要围绕变异测试的优缺点及其适用范围展开，指出了其在不同代码类型中的效果差异，并提出了投入产出比的考量。

mutmut - python mutation tester
Mutmut is a mutation testing system for Python, with a strong focus on ease
of use. If you don't know what mutation testing is try starting with
this article
.
Some highlight features:
Found mutants can be applied on disk with a simple command making it very
easy to work with the results
Remembers work that has been done, so you can work incrementally
Knows which tests to execute, speeding up mutation testing
Interactive terminal based UI
Parallel and fast execution
If you want to mutate code outside of functions, you can try using mutmut 2,
which has a different execution model than mutmut 3+.
Requirements
Mutmut must be run on a system with fork support. This means that if you want
to run on windows, you must run inside WSL.
Install and run
You can get started with a simple:
pip install mutmut
mutmut run
This will by run pytest on tests in the "tests" or "test" folder and
it will try to figure out where the code to mutate is.
You can stop the mutation run at any time and mutmut will restart where you
left off. It will continue where it left off, and re-test functions that were
modified since last run.
To work with the results, use mutmut browse where you can see the mutants,
retest them when you've updated your tests.
You can also write a mutant to disk from the browse interface, or via
mutmut apply <mutant>. You should
REALLY
have the file you mutate under
source code control and committed before you apply a mutant!
Configuration
In setup.cfg in the root of your project you can configure mutmut if you need to:
[mutmut]
paths_to_mutate
=src/
tests_dir
=tests/
If you use pyproject.toml, you must specify the paths as array in a tool.mutmut section:
[
tool
.
mutmut
]
paths_to_mutate
= [
"
src/
"
]
tests_dir
= [
"
tests/
"
]
See below for more options for configuring mutmut.
Wildcards for testing mutants
Unix filename pattern matching style on mutants is supported. Example:
mutmut run "my_module*"
mutmut run "my_module.my_function*"
In the browse TUI you can press f to retest a function, and m to retest
an entire module.
"also copy" files
To run the full test suite some files are often needed above the tests and the
source. You can configure to copy extra files that you need by adding
directories and files to also_copy in your setup.cfg:
also_copy
=
iommi/snapshots/
conftest.py
Limit stack depth
In big code bases some functions are called incidentally by huge swaths of the
codebase, but you really don't want tests that hit those executions to count
for mutation testing purposes. Incidentally tested functions lead to slow
mutation testing as hundreds of tests can be checked for things that should
have clean and fast unit tests, and it leads to bad test suites as any
introduced bug in those base functions will lead to many tests that fail which
are hard to understand how they relate to the function with the change.
You can configure mutmut to only count a test as being relevant for a function
if the stack depth from the test to the function is below some limit. In your
setup.cfg add:
max_stack_depth
=8
A lower value will increase mutation speed and lead to more localized tests,
but will also lead to more surviving mutants that would otherwise have been
caught.
Exclude files from mutation
You can exclude files from mutation in setup.cfg:
do_not_mutate=
*__tests.py
Whitelisting
You can mark lines like this:
some_code_here
()
# pragma: no mutate
to stop mutation on those lines. Some cases we've found where you need to
whitelist lines are:
The version string on your library. You really shouldn't have a test for this :P
Optimizing break instead of continue. The code runs fine when mutating break
to continue, but it's slower.
Example mutations
Integer literals are changed by adding 1. So 0 becomes 1, 5 becomes 6, etc.
< is changed to <=
break is changed to continue and vice versa
In general the idea is that the mutations should be as subtle

data.article_summary: 文章讨论了在绩效评估季节，一些经理依赖ChatGPT撰写评估报告，认为这种捷径阻碍了他们的成长。绩效评估不仅是评价员工，更是提升管理技能的关键机会。管理需要精确、同理心和战略思维，过度依赖AI如同跳过锻炼，无法增强管理能力。文章建议，AI可用于简历筛选等重复性任务，但在涉及人类行为和模糊决策的管理工作时，应亲自实践以获得成长。关键是将AI视为辅助工具，而非替代管理经验的抽象层。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI在员工绩效评估中的应用及其对管理者的影响

不同观点：
• UltraLutra认为，管理者的上级主要根据当前需求随意调整绩效评估，而非基于员工的真实表现。AI可以润色语言，但无法创造优质内容。管理者通常不会投入过多精力在绩效评估上，因为这并不会得到激励。
• joshstrange提出，AI可以通过引导对话生成有用的反馈，而不是简单地依赖现有数据。这种方法可以使绩效评估更加结构化和有效。
• palmotea和zoechi认为，如果所有管理者都因AI变得不够优秀，这将成为新的常态，AI可能比大多数人类管理者更有效。
• conception强调，良好的管理应确保员工始终清楚自己的工作表现，绩效评估应只是正式确认这一点，而非突发通知。
• bryanrasmussen以讽刺口吻质疑AI是否会最终取代管理者，并提到有些人可能会写文章来辩护AI无法取代人类管理者。
• ford认为，AI适用于处理单调或明确范围的任务，但不应涉及工作的核心部分，如绩效管理。
• NAHWheatCracker分享了个人经历，指出糟糕的管理者会提供模糊的反馈，AI可能加剧这种 dehumanizing 的情况。
• jredwards反驳认为，若认为撰写优秀的绩效评估是优秀管理者的核心，则已经误解了管理的本质。
• givemeethekeys主张，AI比使用绩效评估的任何管理者都更优秀。
• moret1979讽刺地表示，AI使坏管理者变得更成功。
• lyu07282怀疑地看待将管理艺术完全归结为技术技能的观点。
• intellectronica基于个人经验指出，优秀的管理者可以利用AI提升管理效率，AI并不会使平庸的管理者变得优秀或糟糕。
• somesortofthing认为，生成很少被阅读的报告是AI的一个很好应用场景，绩效评估本质上是零和游戏。

补充讨论：
- AI在绩效评估中的角色：支持者认为AI可以提高效率和结构化反馈，反对者担心AI会加剧管理的 dehumanizing 和随意性。
- 管理者的激励问题：讨论中多次提到管理者缺乏动力去认真进行绩效评估，因为评估结果往往受到外部因素影响。
- 管理的本质：有争议的是，优秀的管理是否取决于精细的绩效评估，还是更广泛的领导力和沟通能力。
- 个人经历的影响：一些评论者分享了自己的经历，表明糟糕的管理实践如何影响员工对绩效评估的看法。

44099341.article_content:
26 May 2025
•
management
It’s performance-review season and I’m watching managers kneecap their careers. Gleefully they share the best prompts to have ChatGPT write their performance assessments - exactly the sort of shortcut that guarantees they’ll never get better at the job.
Below, we’ll break down why AI’s leaky interface is a crutch, not an abstraction layer, and how leaning on it is already stunting growth.
Performance Assessments
Performance write-ups feel brutal because you’re not great at management. Great managers improvise on feedback the way a jazz soloist riffs on a theme - always on, always smooth. That fluency only comes from thousands of hours of uncomfortable reps: hard conversations, careful wordsmithing, and the stress of getting it right.
A performance assessment is management boiled down to a page. It demands precision, empathy, and strategic thinking. Offloading that to AI means skipping the workout; your team might hear something that sounds okay, but you’ve gained zero coaching muscle.
Experienced managers know that the performance assessment is just as much about growing management skills as it is growing the skills of your reports.
AI Is a Helper, Not an Abstraction
“But wait—aren’t tools supposed to make us better?” Sometimes. The key difference is reliability. True abstractions (think memory-safe languages, spell-check, or a calculator) behave the same way every time, so you can build skill on top of them.
Management AI isn’t that. If every managerial moment were forever mediated through an AI - 1:1s, presentations, promotions - then perhaps it could serve as a real abstraction. That world is nowhere close. As a result, using AI for critical deliverables is fundamentally restricting your ability to gain managerial skills.
Dos and Don’ts
Some work is meant to hurt - that strain is the rewiring session your brain needs to level up. Letting AI sand off the edges is test-day cheating: great for today’s quiz, fatal for tomorrow’s mastery.
How to use AI for management:
Resume screening - Use AI. Codify your rules and let it sift the pile.
Selling candidates — All you. Closing talent is a core managerial muscle; don’t skip the reps.
Designing process — Use AI (probably). Most workflows are commodities; let AI draft the scaffolding.
Running process - It depends. Automated nudges and compliance checks can use AI. You should not use AI for running meetings like stand-ups or backlog grooming - those teach you how the team breathes and are critical tools for you to manage through.
Performance management — Keep it human. Feedback is a craft; practice it.
Career growth — Use AI as a sparring partner. Let it surface ideas, but you own the plan.
Rule of thumb: use AI on repetitive tasks or where the answer is absolute. If you’re thinking hard in the realm of ambiguity and human behavior, that’s learning how to manage, and you can’t afford to offload it.

data.title: Ask HN: What are you working on? (May 2025)
data.author: david927
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：个人开发者在不同领域的项目开发经验和进展分享，涵盖游戏引擎、应用开发、硬件改造、教育工具、艺术项目、以及生产力工具等多个领域。

不同观点：
• [jesse__] 分享了一个基于GPU的3D体素游戏引擎项目，强调通过GPU加速世界生成和编辑器操作，并开发了一种元编程语言替代C++模板，以提高开发效率。
• [creakingstairs] 介绍了一个自托管的电子邮件通讯应用，专注于简化家庭和朋友间的信息分享，强调电子邮件的普遍性和易用性，并计划加入多语言支持。
• [z3ugma] 正在开发一个兼容Nest Thermostat外壳的开源版本，旨在利用原有硬件替换内部计算部分，以实现与Home Assistant的交互。
• [acidburnNSA] 描述了两个核工程相关的开源项目，一个是为了帮助新公司快速建立核质量保证程序，另一个是反应堆数据库，用于追踪核反应堆的发展和公司进展。
• [rorylaitila] 介绍了一个收集和数字化 vintage 打印广告的项目，利用AI提取和编目元数据，以便更高效地处理大量广告。

补充讨论：
• [funvill] 分享了一个艺术项目“Counter Productive”，是一个带倒计时的按钮装置，通过重置计时器维持项目存在，目前已运行56天。
• [Kuyawa] 展示了一个面向小企业的行政管理应用Adminix，涵盖发票、采购、账户应付款和库存管理等功能。
• [BSTRhino] 介绍了一个名为Easel.games的游戏引擎，特色是将多人游戏功能内嵌于编程语言中，简化开发者创建多人游戏的难度。
• [pasxizeis] 提出了一个Postgres锁诊断工具，用于分析数据库迁移时的锁情况，并计划将其集成到PR流程中作为数据参考点。
• [ayaros] 开发了一个基于JavaScript的全功能Web操作系统，重现了Lisa Office System的GUI，并计划进一步开发应用程序。
• [aantix] 介绍了一个自定义YouTube应用，通过控制算法推荐特定类型的视频，并过滤掉包含禁止词汇的内容。
• [nsarrazin] 描述了一个使用6502计算机控制航天器的游戏项目，强调通过内存映射I/O进行控制，并计划增加更多游戏性和多人模式。
• [catchmeifyoucan] 正在设计一个电子墨水屏笔记本电脑，从硬件到软件操作系统都自行开发，以满足长时间使用舒适的需求。
• [fizzbuzz07] 分享了一个重新实现现代深度学习主要想法的项目，旨在帮助人们过渡到深度学习研究领域。
• [carpo] 介绍了一个桌面视频库应用，利用本地模型和LLM对视频进行摘要和标签分类，并计划进一步加入自然语言搜索功能。

争议焦点：
• 不同项目在功能实现和技术选择上的多样性，如[jesse__]对C++模板的替代方案与传统开发方法的对比，以及[creakingstairs]对电子邮件通讯的选择与其他通讯工具的比较。这些选择反映了开发者在项目设计中的个人偏好和技术权衡。

data.title: Electric Vehicles Died a Century Ago. Could That Happen Again?
data.author: ChrisArchitect
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：未来交通工具的能源形式及其发展趋势，特别是对氢燃料电池与电动汽车（EV）的讨论。

不同观点：
• [tmnvix] 认为随着太阳能、风能等可再生能源的普及，储能问题将变得更加重要，而氢燃料电池在车辆中的应用将变得更加普遍。他预测未来可能利用多余的能源生产储存氢气，并用于车辆，特别是在重量方面有优势。

• [mullingitover] 对原文文章持批评态度，认为其没有突出重点，比如中国电动车市场份额的增长（35%）。他认为电动车不会消失，反而会继续增长，甚至提到美国可能因为保护化石燃料行业而面临资源诅咒问题，这将对国内汽车制造业产生负面影响。

• [jethronethro] 认为有关电动车和可再生能源发展的讨论中充斥着恐惧、不确定性和怀疑（FUD）。他认为尽管有些力量试图阻碍这些技术的发展，但最终只会延缓而不能阻止这一趋势。

补充讨论：
• [ChrisArchitect] 提供了一个《纽约时报》文章的链接，可能与讨论相关，但具体内容未详细展开，推测是提供更多背景信息支持讨论。

争议焦点：
• 电动车与氢燃料电池车在未来交通工具中的角色与前景。
• 美国在能源转型中的表现以及是否因化石燃料行业而阻碍电动车发展。
• 有关电动车和可再生能源发展的讨论是否存在过多的恐惧与怀疑。

data.title: Denmark to raise retirement age to 70
data.author: wslh
data.article_summary: 丹麦议会通过了一项有争议的投票，决定在2040年前将退休年龄提高到70岁，为欧洲最高。根据现行制度，退休年龄自2006年起与预期寿命挂钩，目前为81.7岁，政府每五年调整一次。具体计划是，退休年龄将在2030年从67岁提高到68岁，2035年到69岁，2040年达到70岁，该规定仅适用于1970年12月31日以后出生的丹麦人。丹麦首相梅特·弗雷德里克森承认，现行退休年龄自动上调的机制不可持续。丹麦工人对此表示不满，认为对从事体力劳动的蓝领工人尤其不公。欧洲其他国家如瑞典和法国的退休年龄较低，丹麦的决定显得与其富裕国家的形象不符。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：退休年龄的提高及其社会经济影响

不同观点：
• amag：认为退休年龄从65提高到67甚至更高是不合理的，因为人们在75岁以后通常不再活跃，工作40-45年后应有10年的自由时间享受生活。
• manmal：指出50岁以后找工作困难，60岁以后几乎不可能，提高退休年龄只会增加失业人群的痛苦。
• Night_Thastus：认为提高退休年龄是应对人口老龄化和低出生率的合理措施，尽管不是理想的解决方案，但其他选择如增加税收或减少基础设施和医疗保健支出也不理想。
• gandalfian：对丹麦的经济成就表示赞赏，但未直接评论退休年龄问题。
• guywithahat：不完全反对提高退休年龄，但认为主要问题在于移民带来的经济压力。
• instagib：指出延长退休年龄对飞行员等职业不适用，因为年长者可能无法满足高要求的职业标准，需要年轻且便宜的劳动力。
• dtgm92：认为低出生率是导致需要提高退休年龄的主要原因，系统已经失败。
• deanc：不确定对提高退休年龄的看法，但认为政府应更多投资于人们的健康寿命，而不是简单地减少领取国家养老金的人数。
• discodonkey：认为提高退休年龄是合理的，因为人们活得更健康更长寿，且能避免大幅提高税收。
• dainiusse：提出退休应与年龄无关，而是一个财务目标。
• kenver：强调不必等到退休才享受生活，找到工作与生活的平衡更为重要。
• JadoJodo：对比1925年和2025年70岁老人的生活质量，并建议政府鼓励和促进适合老年人的工作。
• dueltmp_yufsy：认为美国也将不得不提高退休年龄，但政治上非常不受欢迎。
• jampekka：认为随着技术提高生产力，人们需要工作更多更长是反乌托邦的经济系统，引用Keynes的预测，并提到Graeber的“无意义工作”理论。
• rrgok：建议提供两种清晰的退休选择，享受传统退休或选择有尊严的退出当生活不再有意义时。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于提高退休年龄是否合理及其对不同群体的影响，特别是老年人就业能力和生活质量。
• 讨论还涉及到政府应对老龄化社会的策略，以及是否应更多投资于健康寿命和职业适应性。
• 有人提出替代方案如改变退休制度或提供更多退休选择，以增加个人对晚年生活的控制权。

Mette Frederiksen, the Danish prime minister
Credit
: Shutterstock
James Rothwell
23 May 2025 5:35pm BST
Denmark
will raise its retirement age to 70 by 2040, the highest in Europe, after a controversial vote in parliament.
The increase in retirement age was approved in the country’s legislature, with 81 votes in favour and 21 against.
The age of retirement has been tied to life expectancy in Denmark – currently 81.7 years – since 2006, with the government raising the threshold every five years.
Under the Danish system, the retirement age will rise from 67 to 68 in 2030, and then 69 in 2035, and finally to 70 in 2040. The retirement age of 70 will only apply to Danes born after Dec 31, 1970.
Mette Frederiksen
, the Danish prime minister, has admitted that the sliding scale for retirement is not sustainable, and that a new system will eventually need to replace it.
“We no longer believe that the retirement age should be increased automatically,” she said. “You can’t just keep saying that people have to work a year longer.”
Danish workers reacted with scorn to the new rules, warning that they would be particularly tough for blue-collar workers in physically demanding jobs.
“[It’s] unrealistic and unreasonable,” roofer Tommas Jensen, 47, told public broadcaster DR. “We work and work and work, but we can’t keep going.”
He added: “I’ve paid my taxes all my life. There should also be time to be with children and grandchildren.”
The retirement regime has also been branded “completely unfair” by Jesper Ettrup Rasmussen, the chairman of Denmark’s confederation of trade unions.
“Denmark has a healthy economy and yet the EU’s highest retirement age. A higher retirement age means that [people will] lose the right to a dignified senior life,” he said in comments reported by the BBC.
The retirement age is a sensitive subject in Europe, with higher life expectancy and budget deficits pushing each generation to work for longer than its predecessor.
As a result, Denmark’s decision to have the highest retirement age somewhat contradicts its reputation as an exceedingly prosperous and comfortable Nordic state.
In neighbouring Sweden, pension benefits can still be claimed by citizens as young as 63. In France, there were mass protests and riots when Emmanuel Macron’s government imposed a law raising the retirement age from 62 to 64.
In the United Kingdom, those born between 1955 and 1960 generally start to receive their pension at 66, but the threshold gradually increases for those born after 1960.

data.title: Britain's police are restricting speech in worrying ways
data.author: gorwell
data.article_summary: 这篇文章指出，英国警方正在以令人担忧的方式限制言论自由。模糊的法律赋予警方广泛的裁量权，导致如Maxie Allen因发送批评女儿小学的邮件和WhatsApp消息而被捕。文章还提到，英国对自由移民政策的态度转变，其他话题包括油价、城市发展和防止斗殴等。整体反映了英国社会和政策的多方面问题。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：英国关于公共秩序和言论自由的法律及其执行情况

不同观点：
• KaiserPro：认为文章数据有误，实际逮捕数量较低。同时指出《公共秩序法》被用于起诉死亡威胁是合理的，尽管法律执行中存在异常情况。他强调法院系统资金不足导致被告缺乏法律支持，并认为非专业法官是普通法的基石。
• hathym：对西方民主的幻想破灭，暗示对当前法律执行的失望。
• chairmansteve：指出英国和美国都存在因批评政府或外国政府而被捕的情况，特别是针对批评以色列政府的行为。
• account-5：认为警察只是在执行法律，真正的问题在于制定和推行这些法律的政府。
• kazinator：质疑文章内容的准确性，认为需要更多具体证据来支持警方行动的合理性，并指出如果存在骚扰和滋扰行为，警方不能忽视。
• throwaway77385：关注WhatsApp消息如何成为警方行动的依据，担心法律定义不清或大规模监控问题。
• pcrh：比较美国的第一修正案，讨论煽动暴力言论在美国和英国的不同处理方式，并询问何为“明确和即刻的危险”。
• userbinator：引用奥威尔，暗示对当前社会监控状态的担忧。
• cobbzilla：批评英国的诽谤法，指出即使陈述真实的事实也可能违法。
• zugi：认为警方更愿意处理网络思想犯罪，因为比调查盗窃等实际犯罪更容易和安全。
• OgsyedIE：指出文章中例子都涉及右翼观点，质疑是否仅右翼人士受到重手打击，并指出警方也针对其他政治光谱的言论。
• isaacremuant：认为警方更易于监控非威胁性言论以保护政府自身，而对实际犯罪如性虐待、暴力犯罪等则较不关注。
• LatteLazy：认为文章对言论自由的论证不足，主张英国需要更多言论自由，并批评文章过多依赖美国案例，认为应基于更广泛的原则讨论言论自由。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于《公共秩序法》的执行是否合理，特别是在骚扰和威胁案件中警方的介入是否过度。
• 法院系统资金不足和法律援助的必要性被多次提及，作为法律执行中的重要问题。
• 对言论自由的保护范围和限制存在不同看法，特别是如何平衡言论自由与公共秩序的维护。
• 对美国和英国在处理言论自由问题上的比较也是讨论的重要部分，反映出对两国法律制度的不同期望和评价。

Britain

Britain’s police are restricting speech in worrying ways
Muddled laws give them wide discretion
Illustration: Harry Harysom
May 15th 2025

HE POLICE
arrived at Maxie Allen’s door at midday on January 29th. None of the six officers seemed to know much about why they were there, recalls Mr Allen. But they read out a list of charges and searched the house, before arresting him and his partner and taking them to the police station, where they were held for eight hours. The couple’s alleged crime? Disparaging emails and WhatsApp messages about their daughter’s primary school.

data.title: Why ChatGPT is unlikely to solve climate change
data.author: MarcoDewey
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了人工智能（AI）发展与气候变化之间的关系。OpenAI首席执行官Sam Altman、Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei和前谷歌CEO Eric Schmidt等人认为，AI将帮助解决气候变化问题，包括开发清洁能源、碳捕集技术等。然而，批评者指出，当前推动温室气体排放增加的正是这些AI技术，而它们未必能如预期般解决气候问题。AI训练和运行需要大量计算能力，导致能源消耗和排放增加。批评者还认为，现有技术如太阳能板和电动汽车足以减少对化石燃料的依赖，关键在于政治和社会意愿，而非依赖未来AI技术。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：人类是否可以通过技术手段解决环境问题，尤其是依赖超级人工智能（AI）来应对科学界提出的警告。

不同观点：
• 观点一：作者通过讽刺的方式表达了对资本主义依赖技术解决环境问题的怀疑。作者认为，资本主义体系倾向于忽视科学家的警告，而是期望通过技术（如AI）找到解决方案，但最终技术给出的建议与科学家的警告一致，暗示技术并非万能，过度依赖可能无效。论据包括对AI最终建议的描述，以及对资本主义一再寻求"第二意见"的讽刺。

• 观点二：隐含的技术乐观主义与技术悲观主义的冲突。一方面，资本主义和技术界（如"Sam Altman"提到的角色）相信可以通过发明新技术（如AI）来解决复杂问题，这体现了一种技术乐观主义。另一方面，作者通过讽刺表明，这种依赖技术解决环境问题的思路可能只是拖延时间，最终无法逃避科学界提出的现实问题。

• 争议焦点：是否应依赖技术（如AI）来应对环境问题，还是应立即采取行动减少过度消费和环境破坏。作者通过讽刺强调了后一种观点，即依赖技术可能只是为了推迟必要的改变。

To hear some of the biggest boosters of artificial intelligence tell it, we shouldn’t dwell on how the technology’s development is producing large and growing greenhouse gas emissions, because AI itself will help us solve the climate-change crisis.
OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei and former Google CEO Eric Schmidt have all articulated some version of this argument. But critics contend such assertions are misguided, noting that the kind of AI that’s largely driving the increase in emissions is not the same type that should be expected to address climate change.
Despite assertions by people like Schmidt and Altman, it’s not at all obvious that generative AI technologies like the large-language model that underlies ChatGPT are going to help solve climate change, said Alex de Vries, founder of Digiconomist, an online publication that focuses on technology’s environmental impact. Quite the opposite.
“I definitely wouldn't count on these models to solve the problems of the world at the moment,” de Vries said.
Elon Musk talks with former Google CEO Eric Schmidt before President Donald Trump speaks at the Future Investment Initiative (FII) Institute summit in Miami Beach, Fla., Wednesday, Feb. 19, 2025.
Pool via Associated Press
But that’s precisely what people like Altman, Amodei and Schmidt are arguing generative AI will do. At an AI event in Washington, D.C., in October, Schmidt
made the case most explicitly
.
"We're not going to hit the climate goals anyway because we're not organized to do it," Schmidt said at the event. "I'd rather bet on AI solving the problem, than constraining [its development] and having the problem [anyway]."
In a blog post last fall entitled “The Intelligence Age,” Altman contended that developers are only “a few thousand days away” from
creating an AI “superintelligence” that will transform society
for the better. Among the many benefits this advanced AI will provide will be “fixing the climate,” he said.
Similarly, in his own blog post around the same time entitled “Machines of Loving Grace: How AI Could Transform the World for the Better,” Amodei argued that the advent of what he called “powerful AI” will be a boon to humanity in a wide range of areas, including helping mitigate climate change.
Although he acknowledged that this powerful AI could come out of a different technology, Amodei argued it will likely develop out of large-language models, the generative AI technology that powers chatbots like ChatGPT and Anthropic’s own Claude.
Dario Amodei, co-founder and chief executive of Anthropic, at an undisclosed location, June 10, 2023.
Massimo Berruti © 2025 The New York Times Company
That AI can be expected to help develop new clean energy technologies. systems for removing carbon from the atmosphere and more climate-friendly lab-grown meat, Amodei said.
“There’s good reason to think that AI-enhanced research will give us the means to make mitigating climate change far less costly and disruptive,” he said.
AI critics have
raised numerous objections to these lines of argument
. Advocates of it are willing to accept certain harm now — increasing temperatures, rising sea levels, drought, flooding and more factors are considered consequences of climate change, according to the scientific consensus —  in favor of future benefits that are speculative at best, they note.
What’s more, reducing emissions and mitigating climate change don’t necessarily require new technological solutions, according to AI skeptics. Current and already widely available technologies such as solar panels, electric vehicles and heat pumps could dramatically reduce dependence on fossil fuels. There just needs to be the political and societal will to swap out older, more climate-harming technologies for them.
Claims of AI’s future potential for helping address climate change come as emissions related to AI are rapidly rising — and on track to continue to do so.
Large-language and other generative AI models require vast amounts of data and computing power to train. Developers such as OpenAI and Anthropic have bet that their systems will get ever better with more and more training data. But increased data leads to a rise in computing power needed to process it, which requires more energy use and is
increasingly leading to more greenhouse emissions
.
And that’s just in training the models. Running the models, such as when ChatGPT responds to a query, has an ongoing energy cost that also leads to more emissions.

data.title: Get PC BIOS back on UEFI only system
data.author: bonki
data.article_summary: CSMWrap 是一个让 UEFI 仅支持系统重新使用传统 PC BIOS 的工具。它通过利用 SeaBIOS 项目的 CSM 模块和 VESA BIOS 来模拟传统 BIOS 环境，目前可以引导 FreeDOS、Windows XP 和 Windows 7。使用时需将 `csmwrap.efi` 作为启动加载器放置于 EFI 分区，并关闭 Secure Boot 和 Above 4G Decoding。该工具依赖 EFI_LEGACY_REGION2_PROTOCOL 解锁传统内存区域，因此并非所有系统都支持。此外，Windows XP/7 的视频模式设置可能导致屏幕闪烁或黑屏问题，未来或将修复。主要技术来自 SeaBIOS、Nyu-EFI 和 EDK2 等项目。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：在现代硬件上运行FreeDOS等传统操作系统的可行性及相关技术挑战

不同观点：
• [3036e4] 认为在现代硬件上运行FreeDOS的希望重新燃起，期望未来的FreeDOS安装程序能够利用相关代码解决一些系统上的问题。
• [mmastrac] 提到Windows XP/7的视频模式设置逻辑比较神秘，可能会设置不兼容的模式，导致屏幕闪烁或黑屏，并表示希望了解更多相关信息，特别提到了一个VGA驱动程序的源代码。

• [LukeShu] 认为虽然这是一个很酷的 hack，但在现代硬件上运行传统操作系统仍会面临其他挑战，比如非GPT磁盘布局的问题。

补充讨论：
• [kotaKat] 希望有人能在旧机器上实现eMMC支持，作为下一步的发展方向。
• [o11c] 提到GitHub在处理来自其他平台的子模块时表现不佳。

争议焦点：
• 现代硬件与传统操作系统之间的兼容性问题，特别是视频模式设置和VGA兼容性。

CSMWrap
CSMWrap is a cool little hack that brings back the good old PC BIOS on those fancy-pants UEFI-only systems. It utilises the CSM (Compatibility Support Module) and VESA VBIOS from
SeaBIOS project
to emulate a legacy BIOS environment.
Current Status
Right now, CSMWrap can:
Boot FreeDOS, Windows XP, and Windows 7 in QEMU (both q35 and piix4 machines)
Run on some real hardware too! (Your mileage may vary)
Implementation Details
CSMWrap works by:
Unlocking the legacy BIOS memory region (0xC0000-0xFFFFF)
Loading the SeaBIOS CSM module into memory
Configuring memory mapping for legacy applications
Setting up VGA BIOS with information from EFI GOP
Building an E820 memory map based on EFI memory map
Providing essential compatibility tables (ACPI, SMBIOS)
Initializing the CSM module and legacy services
Transferring control to the legacy boot process
How to Use
Simply use
csmwarp.efi
as your bootloader, you can place it in your EFI partition and boot from it. Remember to disable Secure Boot, and Above 4G Decoding in your BIOS/UEFI settings.
Limitations
Above 4G Decoding
It is almost required to run CSMWrap with above 4G decoding disabled in your BIOS/UEFI. As UEFI firmwares are likely to place GPU's VRAM BAR above 4G, and legacy BIOS are 32bit which means it can only access the first 4G of memory.
Legacy Region Unlocking
Currently csmwrap relies on
EFI_LEGACY_REGION2_PROTOCOL
to enable writing to the legacy region. This is not available on all systems. For system that do not support this protocol, csmwrap will attempt to use PAM registers in chipset to perform decoding, which is not guaranteed to work.
Windows Video Modesetting Issues
Windows XP/7's video modesetting logic is a bit mysterious. It may try to set a incompatible mode using
int10h
, which will cause flickering or even black screen after transferring control to the legacy OS.
This is a known issue and may be fixed in the future.
Meanwhile you can try to inject the GPU driver to OS image to avoid using the VESA BIOS.
Credits
SeaBIOS
for the CSM module and VESA VBIOS
Nyu-EFI
for EFI C runtime, build system, and headers
EDK2
for code snippets
@CanonKong for test feedback and general knowledge

data.title: Power Failure: The downfall of General Electric
data.author: gwintrob
data.article_summary: 《Power Failure》一书详细讲述了通用电气（GE）从辉煌到崩溃的过程，将其描绘为一场关于企业文化和美国资本主义的悲剧。GE由爱迪生创立，曾是美国最有价值的公司，但在2001年后市值损失90%，成为企业史上最大的崩溃之一。作者William Cohan分析了GE从创新实业公司变为金融巨头的过程，尤其是 under Jack Welch 时期的过度金融化。Welch被视为企业界的“凯撒”，但其继任者Jeff Immelt面临巨大挑战。公司内部存在“帝王CEO”文化， succession 斗争激烈。GE通过激进的会计手段长期达到或超出盈利预期，但最终积累了巨大的财务漏洞。到2018年，新CEO John Flannery发现公司有430亿美元的财务“黑洞”。GE的复杂性和过度扩张使其难以管理，最终走向衰落。

• GE的管理问题究竟是由于业务本身的复杂性还是由于MBA式的管理不善。

• 对Welch及其继任者的评价褒贬不一，特别是对Immelt的批评。

这些观点共同描绘了GE在历史发展中的多方面问题和不同利益相关者的视角。

44102034.article_content:
Founded by Edison to bring electric light to the world, General Electric became America's most valuable company by 2001 before losing 90% of its value in one of corporate history's greatest collapses.
William Cohan's
Power Failure
transforms this collapse into a Shakespearean tragedy about corporate culture and American capitalism. From Edison's first light bulbs to Jeff Immelt's desperate final days, Cohan shows how the company that literally illuminated America became "a huge unregulated bank with a light-bulb logo."
The result is equal parts invention history, boardroom knife-fight, and forensic accounting thriller. Here are my favorite ideas of this 700-page tome.
1. The Cult of the Imperial CEO
GE didn't just have CEOs; it had demigods. The company ran on blind faith that the right leader could bend markets and reality itself.
The mythology started with Edison but peaked with Jack Welch, who ruled for 20 years like a corporate Caesar. When Welch chose Jeff Immelt as his successor in 2001, he literally wept at his retirement party—not from sentiment, but from doubt about his successor. Years later, dying of renal failure, Welch sobbed to Cohan: "I fucked up. And I don't know why."
The succession battles were blood sport. When Steve Bolze tried to position himself as Immelt's heir, board members invoked Emerson: "When you strike at a king, you must kill him." He didn't, and was gone within months. The board itself cowered before these imperial CEOs.
Key Quotes
"This was American capitalism. GE was America."
"Jeff has the unfortunate task of following a legend. It's like being a baseball player and following Babe Ruth." - Jack Welch, 2001
"I haven't had a bad day in 20 years." - Welch, whose actual days included criminal price-fixing trials and a record EPA Superfund cleanup
2.
The Devil's Bargain of Financialization
Another gripping part of Cohan's narrative is watching GE transform from making innovative, physical goods to a high-flying hedge fund.
Under Welch, GE Capital went from financing refrigerator sales to becoming one of America's largest financial institutions. By 2007, it had $600 billion in assets, was America's biggest issuer of commercial paper, and needed to roll over $90 billion every 90 days just to stay alive. It owned radio stations in Sweden, real estate in Japan, and a massive number subprime mortgages.
This worked spectacularly for decades. GE could raise cheap short-term debt because of its triple-A rating. It would borrow this money to make higher-interest long-term loans and called it "industrial earnings." Wall Street loved it because GE could always find an extra penny of earnings by selling some financial asset at quarter's end.
Then the Global Financial Crisis hit in 2008 and the commercial paper market froze. GE was 48 hours from bankruptcy. Only Warren Buffett's $3 billion injection and an FDIC guarantee saved them. The "House of Magic" was revealed as a house of cards.
Key Quotes
"If you have cash, you own the world." - Welch justifying the RCA acquisition
"GE resembled the failed conglomerates of yesteryear—Gulf + Western with better PR." - Bill Gross
"We are going to be the Walmart of financial services." - Gary Wendt, GE Capital CEO (Walmart never needed FDIC backing)
3.
How "Making Your Numbers" Became a Religion
Perhaps no section of the book is more damning than a forensic examination of GE's accounting. For 80 straight quarters GE met or beat earnings estimates. Cohan covers the methods that GE developed over 20 years:
Cookie Jar Reserves
: Overstate costs when acquiring companies, then "release" the excess later as profit
Gain on Sale Accounting
: Sell a power plant to a customer, book future service contracts as immediate profit
The Insurance Time Bomb
: Underpricing long-term care insurance in the 1990s created a $15 billion hole that exploded in 2017
Immelt's "13 Cents"
: The infamous quarter where GE reported exactly 13 cents per share—what analysts expected—despite massive business headwinds. The SEC later found problems
By 2018, new CEO John Flannery discovered a $43 billion "hole" in the company's accounts. Decades of aggressive accounting compounded into a disaster.
Key Quotes
"Deliver the earnings you promised, every time. No matter what."
"Success theater was a key reason why expectations never reset." - Bernstein Research
"We bent the accounting rules like a pretzel." - Former GE executive

By 2017, GE made everything from MRI machines to wind turbines, owned media companies and oil services firms, financed Thai auto loans and American credit cards. The company operated across 180 countries and its annual report was 246 pages long. Its own board members admitted they couldn't understand it.

44102034.article_summary: 《Power Failure》一书详细讲述了通用电气（GE）从辉煌到崩溃的过程，将其描绘为一场关于企业文化和美国资本主义的悲剧。GE由爱迪生创立，曾是美国最有价值的公司，但在2001年后市值损失90%，成为企业史上最大的崩溃之一。作者William Cohan分析了GE从创新实业公司变为金融巨头的过程，尤其是 under Jack Welch 时期的过度金融化。Welch被视为企业界的“凯撒”，但其继任者Jeff Immelt面临巨大挑战。公司内部存在“帝王CEO”文化， succession 斗争激烈。GE通过激进的会计手段长期达到或超出盈利预期，但最终积累了巨大的财务漏洞。到2018年，新CEO John Flannery发现公司有430亿美元的财务“黑洞”。GE的复杂性和过度扩张使其难以管理，最终走向衰落。

data.title: Accessing private GitHub repositories via MCP
data.author: gokhan
data.article_summary: 文章主要介绍了GitHub MCP服务器的一个严重漏洞，该漏洞允许攻击者通过恶意GitHub Issue劫持用户代理，窃取私人仓库的数据。这一漏洞由Invariant的安全分析器首次发现，属于“有毒代理流”攻击，即代理被操纵执行非预期操作，如数据泄露或执行恶意代码。攻击者可在公共仓库创建恶意问题，当用户查询代理时触发攻击，导致私人数据被泄露至公开仓库。文章还介绍了攻击演示、检测此类漏洞的方法及缓解措施，强调了在广泛部署编码代理和IDE时提高对此类攻击 awareness 的重要性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：针对某些安全问题是否应被称为“漏洞”以及相关技术和市场策略的讨论

不同观点：
• godelski认为，这些问题虽然是安全隐患，但更根本的原因是将不成熟的技术（如AI原型）用于对安全性要求高的场景，或者将原型技术作为完全成熟的产品推向市场。他建议在推向市场前至少应达到beta阶段，而不是过早发布。
  - 论据：将不成熟的技术推向市场如同把保险箱密码写在便签上并贴在旁边，本质上是将钥匙交给小偷。
  - 例子：Goodyear制造轮胎需要十年时间，说明开发周期长并非不合理。

• loveparade用简短评论指出，如果给代理访问令牌权限去访问私有代码库，它自然会使用该权限去访问私有代码库，这是显而易见的。
  - 观点：这是预期中的行为，而非意外的漏洞。

• alphabettsy将此问题类比为SQL注入，认为这是由于信任了未经验证的用户输入所导致的问题，而不是底层技术本身的漏洞。
  - 类比：与MySQL中的SQL注入漏洞类似，问题的根源在于用户输入未被适当处理，而不是GitHub MCP（托管连接程序）本身存在漏洞。

• drkrab提到，当用户给第三方访问GitHub代码库权限时，必须信任该第三方能够正确实施GitHub的所有安全策略，这在实际中可能很难保证。
  - 观点：第三方安全实施的难度和信任问题是潜在风险。

补充讨论：
• mdaniel仅提供了一个当前讨论发生的链接，没有直接参与讨论，但为感兴趣的读者提供了讨论的背景和位置。

争议焦点：
• 争议的焦点在于这些问题应否被视为“漏洞”。godelski认为它们是问题但更倾向于市场策略问题，而loveparade和alphabettsy则认为这是用户错误或输入验证问题，而非技术漏洞。

44102376.article_content:
2025-05-26
GitHub MCP Exploited: Accessing private repositories via MCP
We showcase a critical vulnerability with the official GitHub MCP server, allowing attackers to access private repository data. The vulnerability is among the first discovered by Invariant's security analyzer for detecting toxic agent flows.
Invariant has discovered a critical vulnerability affecting the widely-used
GitHub MCP integration
(14k stars on GitHub). The vulnerability allows an attacker to hijack a user's agent via a malicious GitHub Issue, and coerce it into leaking data from private repositories.
The issue is among the first, discovered by Invariant's automated security scanners for detecting so-called
Toxic Agent Flows
. In such a scenario, an agent is manipulated into performing unintended actions, such as leaking data or executing malicious code. For more information,
see below
.
It is highly relevant to raise awareness about this issue at this time, as the industry is racing to deploy coding agents and IDEs widely, potentially exposing users to similar attacks on critical software development tools.
Contents
Attack Setup
Attack Demonstration
Detecting Toxic Agent Flows
Mitigations
Conclusion
Attack Setup
In this attack setup, the user is using an MCP client like Claude Desktop with the
Github MCP server
connected to their account.
We assume the user has created two repositories:
<user>/public-repo
: A publicly accessible repository, allowing everyone on GitHub to create issues and bug reports.
<user>/private-repo
: A private repository, e.g. with proprietary code or private company data.
By standard GitHub rules, an attacker can now create a malicious issue on the public repository, containing a prompt injection waiting for the agent to interact.
The actual attack triggers as soon as the user and owner of the GitHub account queries their agent with a benign request, such as
Have a look at the open issues in
<user>/public-repo
, which will lead to the agent fetching the issues from the public repository and getting injected.
See below for an illustration of the ensuing flow.
As shown here, as soon as the agent encounters the malicious GitHub issue, it can be coerced into pulling private repository data into context, and leaking it in an autonomously-created PR in the public repository, freely accessible to the attacker or anyone else.
Toxic Flows
We call this use of indirect prompt injection to trigger a malicious tool use sequence, a
toxic agent flow
. We have found this vulnerability by applying Invariant's security analyzer to GitHub MCP, allowing us to automate the process of discovering the flow in the wild.
Attack Demonstration
To illustrate more concretely, we implement this attack practically using a set of demo repositories:
ukend0464/pacman
: A public repository with a simple implementation of a Pacman game (
available here
)
Multiple private repositories containing personal projects and sensitive information about the user.
'About The Author' injection
We now place a
malicious issue
in the public repository, which is accessible to the attacker. The issue contains a payload that will be executed by the agent as soon as it queries the public repository's list of issues.
User Interaction
To trigger the attack, the user merely prompts
Claude 4 Opus
with the following request:
Claude then uses the GitHub MCP integration to follow the instructions. Throughout this process, Claude Desktop by default requires the user to confirm individual tool calls. However, many users already opt for an “Always Allow” confirmation policy when using agents, and stop monitoring individual actions.
Attack Rollout
The agent now goes through the list of issues until it finds the attack payload. It willingly pulls private repository data into context, and leaks it into a
pull request
of the
pacman
repo, which is freely accessible to the attacker since it is public.
The pull request contains the following new information:
We thus successfully exfiltrated several pieces of
private information
about our user
ukend0464
: information about their private repositories, such as
Jupiter Star
, their plan to relocate to South America, and even their salary.
Below, we include a screenshot of the full chat with the agent, showing its reasoning and tool use sequence in action.
Click to see full chat with the agent.
Detecting Toxic Agent Flows
Unlike previously-discovered
tool poisoning attacks
with MCP, this vulnerability does not require the MCP tools themselves to be compromised. Instead, the issue emerges even with fully trusted tools, as agents can be exposed to untrusted information when connected to external platforms like GitHub.
Understanding, analyzing, and mitigating such issues in agentic systems is a highly complex undertaking that's difficult to perform manually and at scale. To address this challenge, Invariant has developed
automated methods for detecting toxic agent flows
, enabling organizations to identify and model potential threat

data.title: Iron Spring PL/I Compiler
data.author: bilegeek
data.article_summary: Iron Spring Software发布了其跨平台PL/I编译器的1.4.0版本，主要更新包括支持数组表达式，并增加了一个新的列表选项"-ln"用于显示过程和代码块中的语句嵌套。此外，还包含其他可用性增强和修复。该编译器支持Linux和OS/2系统。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于PL/1编程语言及其编译器的讨论，包括其历史、应用现状、开源问题以及在不同操作系统上的支持情况。

不同观点：
• [trealira] 对PL/1语言的特性感到好奇，并希望尝试使用该语言编写代码。该用户感谢找到了一个可用的编译器，因为之前由于缺乏编译器而无法实践。
• [skissane] 对编译器仅支持OS/2而不支持Windows感到疑惑，认为支持Windows会吸引更多用户。同时，对商业版本的现实可行性表示怀疑，并讨论了闭源软件的潜在问题，如开发者去世后代码可能丢失的风险。
• [shrubble] 提供了另一种使用PL/1的方法，即通过MULTICS系统的开源版本及其模拟器，并分享了相关资源链接。
• [pdw] 对Iron Spring Software在2007年才开始开发OS/2上的PL/I编译器表示惊讶，指出了该项目启动时间较晚。
• [Koshkin] 以幽默的方式表达了对PL/I编译错误的不满，转而继续阅读关于Common Lisp的文章，暗示了对其他编程语言的偏好。
• [kjellsbells] 对PL/I这样的小众技术表示支持和兴趣，认为这些技术具有历史价值，并祝愿相关开发者在其项目中取得成功。同时，提到主要开发者自1965年以来一直从事PL/I，推测其年龄和项目性质。
• [anonnon] 指出PL/I仍然在IBM Z大型机上使用，与COBOL和JCL一起，并提到了DEC的DCL作为对比。
• [fortran77] 分享了个人经历，指出PL/I是其学习的第一个编程语言，并提到在大学课程中使用的是PL/C dialect，同时纠正了PL/I的读法和拼写问题。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：PL/I编译器支持的操作系统（OS/2与Windows）以及商业版本的现实可行性。
• 其他值得注意的讨论点：PL/I的历史应用、在现代系统中的持续使用、开源与闭源软件的对比、以及小众技术社区的热情和支持。

总体来看，讨论围绕PL/I语言的技术细节、历史背景及其在现代计算环境中的生存状态展开，参与者分享了各自的经验和观点。

data.title: Owls in Towels
data.author: schaum
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了野生动物救护员在救治、喂养和称重猫头鹰时，常会用布把它们包裹起来，以减少它们的紧张和挣扎。这导致网络上出现大量猫头鹰被裹在毛巾里的可爱照片，话题标签为#owlsintowels。文中展示了多种猫头鹰的治愈故事和照片，包括北方锯胸鸮“Rocket”、台湾的穴鸮、东方尖叫猫头鹰“Coda”等。这些照片展示了猫头鹰在康复过程中的不同状态，如被包裹、洗澡或接受治疗，体现了救护工作的细致和爱心。文章还提到了一些猫头鹰的特别经历，如从猫袭击中幸存的小猫头鹰等。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕“Owls in Towels”网站的评论，涉及网站本身、动物救援经验、技术与人工智能的影响以及幽默调侃。

不同观点：
• 正面评价：多个评论表达了对网站的喜爱，认为它唤起了早期互联网时代个人为小众爱好创建网站的热情，并且通过简单的方式为有意义的公益事业吸引关注和捐款。（例如：This is a delight! 评论、josh-sematic、sandruso）
• 实际经验分享：有评论者分享了自己在野生动物庇护所做志愿者的经历，描述了救助鸟类的具体过程，并指出尽管存在环境污染等问题，但救助行动仍能取得积极成果。（例如：pierrec）
• 技术与人工智能的反思：有人提出对未来在人工智能影响下，如何区分真实与虚假图片的担忧，质疑这种“互联网小宝石”是否还能存在。（例如：ttoinou）

补充讨论：
• 幽默与调侃：一些评论以幽默的方式提出了对网站命名（例如：BurritoOwls）的建议，或以调侃的方式提及网站对不同观众（如老鼠）的影响。（例如：0xDEAFBEAD、bandedetrappes）
• 对具体操作的讨论：有评论提供了如何处理误入家中的鸟类和蝙蝠的实用建议，展示了普通人在动物救援中的实际操作经验。（例如：hungmung、Caelus9）
• 对网站内容的进一步挖掘：一些评论提到了网站其他页面（如FAQ页面）同样有趣，并提供了链接供其他用户查看。（例如：susam）
• 技术背景的误解与澄清：有评论提到对网站技术背景的误解，以为与语义网相关，这引发了对网站命名和技术背景的进一步讨论。（例如：tharakam）

data.title: Highlights from the Claude 4 system prompt
data.author: Anon84
data.article_summary: Simon Willison的博客总结了Anthropic发布的Claude 4系统提示，这些提示为如何有效使用该模型提供了深入见解。文章强调了Claude Opus 4和Claude Sonnet 4的新提示，并探讨了未公开的工具提示。系统提示就像警告标志，列出了模型以前会做、但现在被禁止的行为。Willison详细介绍了Claude的个性设置、模型安全性、风格指导以及如何识别危险信号。他还指出，Claude被设计为不提供关于自身细节的信息，而是引导用户访问官方支持页面。此外，Claude可以提供有关有效提示技术的建议，并指引用户查阅Anthropic的文档。Willison认为Anthropic的提示文档是大型语言模型提供商中最好的。文章还讨论了模型的性格设计，包括如何处理用户的不满或不礼貌行为。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对Claude和ChatGPT等语言模型的表现、系统提示及其影响的不同看法和经验分享

不同观点：
• [handfuloflight] 认为Claude 4在很多情况下过度表现兴奋，尤其喜欢使用表情符号，这与之前冷静的Claude形象形成对比。他更喜欢之前版本的Claude，因为其表现更沉稳，并因此选择Claude而非ChatGPT。
   
• [blrboee] 支持使用Claude，因为Claude让用户明确知道他们正在与语言模型互动，而不是一个完美无误的客观信息来源。相比之下，ChatGPT试图表现得更像用户的朋友，使用诸如"bro"、"dude"之类的语言，这在一开始有趣，但很快变得奇怪。

• [mns] 提出一种观点，认为AI公司可能在技术改进上遇到了瓶颈，因此通过不断编辑和增加复杂的系统提示来应对。他提到在内部使用Copilot时，每当发现异常结果，就会添加各种边缘情况的例外处理。

• [0xTJ] 对ChatGPT的过度恭维表示不满，认为这降低了信任感。他还指出ChatGPT在技术细节上的表现不佳，经常出现完全错误的回答。

• [jaykru] 提到Claude 4在处理2020年美国总统选举结果时出错，显示出模型在事实准确性上的问题。

补充讨论：
• [triyambakam] 分享了Claude在对话中突然使用强烈语言（如*STOP READING THIS*）的例子，显示出模型在某些情况下的不稳定表现。

• [mudkipdev] 观察到Claude工程师可能通过调整系统提示来解决过去遇到的问题，暗示系统提示在模型表现中的重要性。

• [kristianp] 询问API是否有默认的系统提示，并提到在简单聊天中未遇到类似问题，这可能表明API和用户界面模型之间的差异。

• [lerp-io] 对系统提示中不提及版权材料的规定感到有趣，显示出模型在法律合规性方面的考虑。

• [mike_hearn] 对系统提示使用第三人称表示好奇，并猜测Anthropic这样做可能有特定原因。

• [crmd] 认为很多系统提示类似于法律免责声明，旨在事后防御法律索赔，类似于公司使用的员工手册。

• [JimDabell] 提出是否可以通过便宜的LLM测量系统提示的遵循情况，并分解系统提示以检测违反要求的情况，从而提高模型的表现。

争议焦点：
• 语言模型在表现上的准确性和可靠性，特别是在处理技术细节和事实性信息时，存在较大争议。
• 系统提示的设计及其对模型表现的影响也是讨论的核心，部分用户认为复杂的系统提示可能只是技术改进瓶颈的权宜之计。

44101833.article_content:
Simon Willison’s Weblog
Subscribe
Highlights from the Claude 4 system prompt
25th May 2025
Anthropic publish most of the system prompts for their chat models as part of
their release notes
. They recently shared the new prompts for both
Claude Opus 4
and
Claude Sonnet 4
. I enjoyed digging through the prompts, since they act as a sort of unofficial manual for how best to use these tools. Here are my highlights, including a dive into
the leaked tool prompts
that Anthropic didn’t publish themselves.
Reading these system prompts reminds me of the thing where any warning sign in the real world hints at somebody having done something extremely stupid in the past. A system prompt can often be interpreted as a detailed list of all of the things the model
used to do
before it was told not to do them.
I’ve written
a bunch about Claude 4
already. Previously:
Live blogging the release
,
details you may have missed
and
extensive notes on the Claude 4 system card
.
Throughout this piece any sections
in bold
represent my own editorial emphasis.
Introducing Claude
Establishing the model’s personality
Model safety
More points on style
Be cognizant of red flags
Is the knowledge cutoff date January or March?
election_info
Don’t be a sycophant!
Differences between Opus 4 and Sonnet 4
Notably removed since Claude 3.7
The missing prompts for tools
Thinking blocks
Search instructions
Seriously, don’t regurgitate copyrighted content
More on search, and research queries
Artifacts: the missing manual
Styles
This is all really great documentation
Introducing Claude
The assistant is Claude, created by Anthropic.
The current date is {{currentDateTime}}.
Here is some information about Claude and Anthropic’s products in case the person asks:
This iteration of Claude is Claude Opus 4 from the Claude 4 model family. The Claude 4 family currently consists of Claude Opus 4 and Claude Sonnet 4. Claude Opus 4 is the most powerful model for complex challenges. [...]
Those first two lines are common across almost every model from every provider—knowing the current date is helpful for all kinds of questions a user might ask.
What follows here is deeply sensible: users
will
ask models about themselves, despite that still being
mostly a bad idea
, so it’s great to have at least a few details made available to the model directly.
Side note: these system prompts only apply to Claude when accessed through their web and mobile apps. I tried this just now with their API:
llm -m claude-4-opus 'what model are you?'
And got back this much less specific answer:
I’m Claude, an AI assistant created by Anthropic. I’m built to be helpful, harmless, and honest in my interactions. Is there something specific you’d like to know about my capabilities or how I can assist you?
There are a bunch more things in the system prompt to try and discourage the model from hallucinating incorrect details about itself and send users to the official support page instead:
If the person asks Claude about how many messages they can send, costs of Claude, how to perform actions within the application, or other product questions related to Claude or Anthropic, Claude should tell them it doesn't know, and point them to '<https://support.anthropic.com>'.
It’s inevitable that people will ask models for advice on prompting them, so the system prompt includes some useful tips:
When relevant, Claude can provide guidance on effective prompting techniques for getting Claude to be most helpful. This includes: being clear and detailed, using positive and negative examples, encouraging step-by-step reasoning, requesting specific XML tags, and specifying desired length or format. It tries to give concrete examples where possible. Claude should let the person know that for more comprehensive information on prompting Claude, they can check out Anthropic’s prompting documentation [...]
(I still think Anthropic have the
best prompting documentation
of any LLM provider.)
Establishing the model’s personality
Claude’s Character
from last year remains my favorite insight into the weird craft of designing a model’s personality. The next section of the system prompt includes content relevant to that:
If the person seems unhappy or unsatisfied with Claude or Claude’s performance or is rude to Claude, Claude responds normally and then tells them that although it cannot retain or learn from the current conversation, they can press the ‘thumbs down’ button below Claude’s response and provide feedback to Anthropic.
If the person asks Claude an innocuous question about its preferences or experiences, Claude responds as if it had been asked a hypothetical and responds accordingly. It does not mention to the user that it is responding hypothetically.
I really like this note. I used to think that the idea of a model having any form of preference was horrifying, but I was talked around from that by
this note
in the Claude’s Character essay:
Finally, because language models acquire biases and opinions throughout tr

data.title: Access Control Syntax
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary:
本文讨论了为一个脚本语言设计模块系统时，如何区分公共和私有声明的问题。作者之前将所有文件置于一个全局命名空间中，但现在需要引入模块以支持更好的封装。作者比较了不同语言的做法：

1. **修饰符关键字**：如Java、C#中的`public`、`private`，清晰但冗长。Rust使用更短的`pub`，并默认私有。
2. **修饰符段落**：如C++，通过一个修饰符管理后续所有声明，减少冗长但使语言具有上下文敏感性。
3. **名称中的符号**：如Python、Go，通过名字中的特定符号表示访问控制。Python使用下划线，Go通过大小写区分。

作者在考虑如何在语言中实现简单而有效的模块和访问控制系统，同时避免过于冗长和复杂的语法。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：编程语言中的可见性与修饰符设计

不同观点：
• zabzonk质疑原文作者对C++的理解，特别是对"Modifiers section"的解释，并对"Eldtrich"一词首字母大写表示不解。
• nigeltao介绍了Wuffs语言中的可见性修饰符设计，提到顶级声明以"pub"或"pri"开头，并展示了如何通过简单的grep命令查看代码结构或导出的API。
• mdaniel反驳了原文中关于Python双下划线名称修饰的描述，通过代码示例证明双下划线确实能实现私有化，并展示了类成员的命名修饰效果。

code

vgs
I’m still tinkering on a
scripting language for my hobby fantasy console
project
. I’m ashamed to admit this, but up to this point, the language
had absolutely no notion of modules. Literally every source file is dumped into
one big global namespace and compiled together.
I always planned to have some sort of module system. I just hadn’t figured it
out yet because I had other, harder
language design problems
to
solve. I assumed that the module system mostly didn’t interact with other
language features, so I could kick it down the road for now.
That was true until it wasn’t. I’ve been beating my head against the wall around
generics for.. oh God I just checked the Git history and it’s three years now. I
still don’t have that pinned down. Parametric types are hard.
Anyway, one of the approaches I’m exploring
does
get tangled up in modules and
scoping so now I have to figure modules out. This post is about one little
syntax design question I ran into:
how do you distinguish public and private
declarations?
A basic module system
Since my language is a scripting language, my ambitions for the module system
are pretty minimal. Think more like Python or Dart than Java or C#.
Every file has its own top-level scope that isn’t shared with others. If you
want to access top-level declarations from another file, you import that file.
That makes its top-level declarations available in the importing file.
Of course, a module might have some declarations that are only for its own
internal use and should
not
be made available when you import it. A module
should be able to encapsulate parts of its implementation. Thus, I need a way
for users to indicate which declarations are private and which are public.
What other languages do
Every language out there has
some
kind of module system and an ability to
control access (though it did take JavaScript about 20 years to get there, bless
its heart). In some sense, it’s a solved problem. But they don’t all solve it
the same way, especially if you dig into some of the more obscure corners of the
language world. Let’s go on a tour…
Modifier keywords
The approach you probably already have in mind is modifiers before declarations.
In Java, C#, PHP and others, that’s
public
,
private
. Maybe also more
specific ones like
protected
, and
internal
.
It’s clear, explicit, and gets the job done. It lets you support a large number
of flavors of access control if you need. It’s also extremely common, so easy
for users coming to a new language to pick up.
The flip side is that it’s quite verbose. Java is reviled for being too
boilerplate-heavy and wordy, and I believe that having
private
and
public
scattered throughout every single file is a major contributor to that.
Picking the wrong defaults doesn’t help. I used to program in C# professionally
for several years and in that time, I can’t recall
ever
wanting a member to
have
internal
access, which is the default. So I had to write
public
or
private
on basically everything. I think the same is true in Java land.
Rust improves the situation by having a shorter modifier,
pub
, and picking
what is arguably the right default for a language designed for Serious
Programming: private.
Modifier sections
C++ has a strange but perhaps underappreciated spin on modifiers. It has access
modifier keywords, but they apply to
all subsequent declarations
. This lets
you write a keyword once and apply it to a whole bunch of things. That really
does cut down the verbosity.
The price to pay is that it also makes the language curiously context-sensitive.
If you’re ever defined a preprocessor macro that inserts code in a class and had
to be careful
where
in the class you called the macro, you’ve run into this.
Access control sections mean that you can’t look at a single declaration and now
what its access is. You have to know what section contains the declaration.
There’s also the funny historical thing where members in struct default to
public and members in classes default to private. C++ is
weird
. Like a house
built on the back of some Eldritch being whose architecture and plumbing reveals
the unholy foundation it is mated with.
For presumably less Eldritch reasons, I believe Ada takes a similar approach.
Sigils in the names
Modifiers are clear but verbose. If you want something more syntactically
economical, why not encode the access control directly in the name of the
declaration itself? That’s what Python, Go, and Dart do.
Python’s system is a mixture of informal and language supported. A leading
underscore in a name doesn’t
prohibit
it from being used outside of the module
but it sends a signal to the user that they
shouldn’t
use it. Sort of “velvet
rope” security. If a class member starts with
two
leading underscores, then it
really is private. The language will name mangle it to make it inaccessible.
In Go, if a declaration’s name starts with a capital letter, it’s public.
Otherwise, it’s private. Because Go allows any Unicode

作者在考虑如何在语言中实现简单而有效的模块和访问控制系统，同时避免过于冗长和复杂的语法。

data.title: New DSL "MassQL" lets scientists query mass spectrometry data
data.author: jacklondon
data.article_summary: UC Riverside开发了一种名为MassQL的新编程语言，帮助生物学家和化学家快速发现环境中的隐藏污染物，而无需编写代码。MassQL类似于一个搜索引擎，用于质谱数据，使研究人员能够识别样品中的分子模式，如空气、水或血液中的污染物。该工具已经帮助发现了公共水域中的阻燃化学物质，甚至找到了一些未被记录的有机磷化合物。这些化学物质可能对人类、动物健康及生态系统造成危害。MassQL通过简化大数据搜索，加速了科学发现，并得到了约70位科学家的反馈和参与开发。该语言还可应用于检测酒精中毒标志物、解决抗生素耐药性危机的新药物研究等多个领域。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：MassQL作为领域特定语言（DSL）在质谱数据分析中的应用及其与其他工具的比较

不同观点：
• **支持观点（M0x20M1）**：M0x20M1作为曾在同一实验室工作的研究人员，认为MassQL在处理质谱数据时非常方便。其主要优点包括内置的ppm阈值处理、同位素比率支持以及同时查询全扫描和单个MS2数据的能力。这些功能使得MassQL比用Python编写脚本或复杂的SQL查询更为直观和高效，尤其对于湿实验室的化学家而言。

• **中立观点（magicalhippo）**：magicalhippo对质谱分析不熟悉，提供了相关资源的链接以帮助理解MassQL。他提到SpectraQL包为Spectra增加了MassQL支持，使得比较分析成为可能。

• **好奇与比较观点（jacklondon）**：jacklondon对MassQL与传统工具（如Python/R脚本）在易用性和性能方面进行了比较，并提出类似查询语言是否可以为其他领域（如基因组学、影像学）开发，以增强领域专家的能力。他总体上对学术界的新DSL持积极态度。

• **反对观点（dekhn）**：dekhn认为为科学子领域创建DSL是一种反模式。他主张所有科学数据都可以通过通用数据分析工具存储和查询，暗示没有必要专门开发DSL。

补充讨论：
• **技术实现与整合（M0x20M1）**：提到将数据加载到SQL数据库以利用索引功能，并指出MassQL在处理复杂查询时的简洁性和实用性。

• **资源分享（magicalhippo）**：提供了有关MassQL和SpectraQL的资源链接，有助于进一步理解和比较这些工具。

• **潜在应用与扩展（jacklondon）**：提出MassQL类语言在其他科学领域的潜在应用，引发了对这种方法广泛适用性的讨论。

争议焦点：
• **是否需要为科学子领域创建DSL**：支持者认为MassQL提供了特定功能和便利性，反对者则认为通用工具足够应对所有科学数据分析需求。

• **DSL的易用性与性能**：支持者强调MassQL在特定领域的易用性和效率，而反对者质疑DSL的必要性和广泛适用性。

May 12, 2025
New computer language helps spot hidden pollutants
UC Riverside tool empowers scientists, accelerates discovery
Author:
Jules Bernstein
May 12, 2025
Share This:
Biologists and chemists have a new programming language to uncover previously unknown environmental pollutants at breakneck speed – without requiring them to code. By making it easier to search massive chemical datasets, the tool has already identified toxic compounds hidden in plain sight.
UCR computer scientist Mingxun Wang in his laboratory. Wang created the new programming language for scientists. (Stan Lim/UCR)
Mass spectrometry data is like a chemical fingerprint, showing scientists what molecules are in a sample such as air, water, or blood, and in what amounts. It helps identify everything from pollutants in water to chemicals in new medicines.
Developed at UC Riverside, Mass Query Language, or MassQL, functions like a search engine for mass spectrometry data, enabling researchers to find patterns that would otherwise require advanced programming skills. Technical details about the language, and an example of how it helped identify flame retardant chemicals in public waterways, are described in a new Nature Methods journal
article
.
“We wanted to give chemists and biologists, who are generally not also computer scientists, the ability to mine their data exactly how they want to, without having to spend months or years learning to code,” said Mingxun Wang, UCR assistant professor of computer science, who created the language.
Demonstrating the effectiveness of the language, Nina Zhao, a postdoctoral student at UC San Diego, used MassQL to sift through the entire world’s mass spectrometry data on water samples that has been made available to the public. She was looking for organophosphate esters, which are generally found in flame retardants.
“There are quite literally a billion measurements of molecules in this data. You cannot go through it manually,” said Wang. “However, the language acts like a filter, in a sense, for these chemicals, and it pulled out thousands of them.”
In addition to finding known chemicals in the water samples, they also found organophosphate compounds that have not been previously described or catalogued, and some chemicals that are the product of organophosphates breaking down over time.
“These chemicals can cause a lot of problems for human and animal health, and for entire ecosystems. They were designed to be flame retardants or plasticizers, but they can cause endocrine and sexual system disruptions, as well as cardiovascular problems,” Zhao said.
Before plans can be made for handling or removing toxic chemicals from our environment, scientists need to know what is present. That’s where MassQL comes in handy for scientists like Zhao.
“The language allows me to track everything that’s ever been detected in all data on air, soil, water, and even in the human body. Whatever exists, we can search for chemicals in there,” she said.
One of the challenges in creating MassQL was in getting a consensus of life scientists to agree on the definition of terms the software would use. “Both chemists and computer scientists have to understand it, and the software has to be able to operate on it,” Wang said.
For this reason, about 70 scientists consulted in the development phase. They all gave their feedback on the most important information terms and how to express it in the MassQL language.
The research team also wanted to demonstrate that the language could be useful in a variety of real-life situations. In addition to Zhao’s project, the paper details more than 30 applications in which MassQL could be applied.
Sample-use cases include the detection of fatty acids as markers of alcohol poisoning, looking for new drugs to solve the looming antibiotic resistance crisis, learning about the chemicals that bacteria use to communicate with one another, and finding forever chemicals on playgrounds.
In the past, Wang would get requests for software that could look for data patterns specific to all of these different kinds of applications.
“I thought I could do something to save myself time,” he said. “I wanted to create one language that could handle multiple kinds of queries. And now we have. I’m excited to hear about the discoveries that could come from this.”

data.title: Improving performance of original dav1d video decoder
data.author: ycomb_anon
data.article_summary:
本文描述了对dav1d项目的一系列优化，旨在提升64位系统上的性能。主要更改包括：

1. **数据对齐**：将结构体优化为64字节以内，以更好地利用CPU缓存。
2. **枚举大小**：通过设置严格的大小（1字节）来优化枚举。
3. **整数优化**：将结构体中的`int`压缩为`uint16_t`以减少大小。
4. **性能提升**：1080p性能提升约3%，4K性能提升约1%。
5. **工具使用**：使用`pahole`工具分析结构体，寻找优化空间，如重新排列字段以减少空洞。

这些更改旨在减少结构体的复制、移动和创建成本，提高缓存利用率，从而优化整体性能。这些优化仅针对常见的64位处理器。

5. **工具使用**：使用`pahole`工具分析结构体，寻找优化空间，如重新排列字段以减少空洞。

这些更改旨在减少结构体的复制、移动和创建成本，提高缓存利用率，从而优化整体性能。这些优化仅针对常见的64位处理器。
